text: [founder] Every hero loads in as one orchestrated Framer Motion timeline on Kaching's motion tokens (`ease.reveal [.26,.32,.14,1]` 1.2s travel + 0.9s fade, 70ms stagger, 6px blur on text only, stage lifts from 97%, controls 220ms `outQuint`): frame lines draw, then nav (it animates too), then headline word by word, subtitle, CTAs, then the product stage, then its contents in reading order, then decorative tiles and routes. Nothing is visible before its moment: connection dots appear only when their route lands, and only then do pulses and comets start. Hover states slide (shared `layoutId` pills in nav, segmented controls, sidebars). Reduced motion shows everything in place.
why: Founder on Kestrel round 5: "the blue dots that connect, why are they always visible, no animation, plus nav bar too? make everything smooth using framer motion", "make the entire load-in smoother with stagger... check how we have Kaching".
check: a frame at ~0.4s shows only the frame; no element with a looping animation is visible before its entrance; all delays come from one timeline object; tokens live in one `motion.ts`. Also check the nav and tiles are clickable (no transparent layer above them).
origin: founder

text: [founder] Looping accents (pulse rings, pings, comets) must be invisible until their moment: start every looping keyframe array at opacity 0 (`opacity: [0, 0.4, 0]`, `times: [0, 0.05, 1]`) or wrap the loop in a group that enters at that moment. Framer Motion paints the first keyframe during the delay, so `opacity: [0.4, 0]` shows a static dot from page load. Order effects as cause then effect: the note lands, its connector draws, the target line lights up and the dot lands as the connector arrives, then the pulse starts.
why: Founder on Margin build 1: "the red bubble doesn't fade in, it just stays there when loading in, very distracting".
check: filmstrip at 300ms steps: no looping element visible before its entrance; grep `animate={{ .*opacity: \[0\.[1-9]` for loops starting visible.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Do not ship the generic "everything loads in" parade (every word, block and row rising out of blur in sequence). Choreograph the load-in around the brand's idea with ONE conceptual reveal (dawn light sweeping across a dark product, ink developing on paper, a flow drawing itself), and keep the rest either present at first paint or arriving in at most 2-3 quick groups within ~1.2s. Word-by-word headline reveals are a deliberate choice for one brand, not the default. Vary the motion vocabulary per brand exactly like layout and type.
why: Founder on Nocturne: "not up to our quality levels... everything is just loading in and it's a bit noobish". Kestrel's load-in was praised once; repeating the same kit stagger on Margin, Strata and Nocturne turned it into a template. Research agrees: 8 of 15 top heroes show the headline in the first frame and the median hero settles in ~1.5s (knowledge/web/product-motion-patterns.md).
check: filmstrip at 0/300/800/1500ms: the composed hero (headline + CTA) is readable by 300ms unless the concept needs otherwise; entrance groups <= 3; DIRECTION.md names the conceptual reveal and how it differs from the last build's.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Every product visual on one site speaks ONE visual language: one edge treatment for white boxes (a 1px hairline OR a faint 6% ring, never both, never a borderless box with a muddy shadow), one radius ladder by element height (nested radius = outer minus inset), one grey shadow scale of at most 3 levels, type roles at 500/600 only, one accent rule (accent only for the selected/primary thing, tints at ~8%). Benchmark is Commslayer/Attio product UI. Audit computed values across ALL visuals before shipping, not one at a time.
why: Founder on the Kaching app visuals (2026-10-09): "the animations are in 3 completely different styles of colours, effects, roundness... what the hell", "random box components without borders and bad shadows or double pixel stroke"; client: "I saw 3-4 different styles of borders and how things look and move". Root cause found in code: three competing box-shadow recipes in one style file.
applies: every animated product visual / bento scene / card.
check: across all visuals: distinct box-shadow strings <= 3, no element with both a border and a 0 0 0 1px ring, distinct radii map to the ladder, font weights in {500, 600}.

text: [founder] Product photos inside an app/section visual are tinted from that section's own palette (or neutral grey); a red tee glowing on the green Cart card is wrong. Palettes stay clean: gold is a clean amber, never olive or muddy.
why: Client: "why does the red T-shirt glow on the green card instead of being green", "the yellow is too dirty compared to the new one".
applies: dithered/duotone product art and app colour fields.
check: each product-art ramp's hue sits within ~25deg of its section accent or is neutral.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Dither (and gradient) fields should end in a slow, uneven, drifting wave, not one straight horizontal line, and the wave stays modest: depth about a quarter of the fade band, capped near 85px, wavelength ~640px. 0.36 of the band / 120px cap read "good but a bit too big".
why: Client: "make some waves so it's not all one straight horizontal line, it looks basic"; founder after the first pass: "they're good but just a bit too big".
check: the fade boundary varies along its length; peak depth <= ~86px at 1440.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Never reproduce a friend brand's signature section identically (Kaching's founders' letter mirrored Commslayer's structure and was rejected); take the idea, then make it unmistakably ours (Kaching: a torn notebook page with 2px dither fibres along the tear).
why: Client: "it's not similar, it's identical to Commslayer, I'll be ashamed to look their founder in the eye".
check: structure, material and copy rhythm all differ from the reference.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Hero title sizes are one scale across a site's secondary pages; no page gets a one-off giant h1 (Kaching About was "huge and out of place").
check: h1 font-size is identical across secondary pages at each breakpoint.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Auto-advancing tabs show progress as a small circular ring beside the active label (or a fill inside a full-width segmented track), never a 1px line under a pill.
why: Client: "that 1px line at the bottom of the pill doesn't look good, try a small circular progress next to the name".
check: no progress hairline under pills; the indicator is driven by the same clock as the advance.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Product dashboards default to the compact, calm grammar measured from Rico's and Kargul's real screens (knowledge/web/heyrico-recreation-lessons.md, kargul-source-study.md), not to a "spacious AlignUI template" reading: one size smaller than instinct everywhere (sidebar ~260px, rows 28-30px on a 30-32px pitch, controls 28-30px, icons 14px stroke at text size, labels 13-14px, KPI numbers ~18px semibold-tabular, card padding 16px, page gutters 24px); hierarchy from two text greys, not from size or weight; group labels small and sentence case, never uppercase; active nav row = grey fill + darker text only (no accent bar or chevron); canvas and sidebar share one neutral, cards are white with a 1px border and no shadow (one shadow per screen at most); the accent appears only in data (bars, lines, meters, progress); tight inside, generous between (2px between rows, 20px between cards). Build one primary view to full detail with real-looking data and working interactions, and put secondary content in overlays (sheets, popovers, dialogs) instead of stacking six blocks.
why: Founder rejected Acquisity v1 (boxed, colourful, cramped) and v2 (an "AlignUI template" reading with uppercase labels, 24px numbers, 32px padding): "it copied it mostly and just changed surface level stuff... nothing like Marcel Kargul's style nor Rico... too noobish... nothing like Attio". Recreating Rico 1:1 and auditing Kargul's code showed the engine's product UI is one notch too big, too many sizes (7 type sizes vs 3, 5 control heights vs 1, 8 radii vs 4) and too boxy.
check: distinct font sizes in the main view <= 4; one control height for actions; icon size = adjacent text size; shadows <= 1 per screen; no uppercase group labels; overlay side-by-side with a Rico/Kargul reference via tools/compare.mjs.
source: founder verdicts on Acquisity v1/v2; Rico recreation and Kargul source study, 2026-10-09
origin: founder

text: [founder] A content reference (an existing screen, a kit, a brief) is content only: redesign structure, sizes and hierarchy from scratch in our own system, and add what the product is missing (sections, states, live elements) instead of re-skinning the original layout box for box.
why: Founder: "that example I gave you was just like the content, you should design the stuff in your own size and way or even add stuff there isn't and just do it consistently".
check: DIRECTION.md lists what was restructured and what was added, not only what was restyled.
origin: founder

text: [founder] The product-UI bar is Marcel Kargul's, Rico's (@_heyrico) and Attio's shipped product work, not "AlignUI-flavoured". Before building product UI, study and recreate reference screens at 1:1 (overlay your render on the reference and close the gaps), build from a measured product kit, and judge every screen side by side with a reference at the same zoom. A redesign that keeps the source layout and changes surface styling is a reject.
why: Founder on Acquisity v1/v2: "it seems to have copied it mostly and just changed surface level stuff", "nothing like Marcel Kargul's style nor Rico... too noobish... nothing like Attio... spend more time perfecting product craft".
applies: all SaaS app UI and dashboards.
check: DIRECTION.md names the reference screens used, includes a side-by-side at equal zoom, and lists the structural changes (not only restyling).
origin: founder

text: [founder] Bento visuals (Commslayer-measured): no grey stage boxes; each visual starts exactly on its copy's left edge, one fixed gap under the copy, top-aligned (never centred in a tall box), filling the cell's width; only the lead cell carries the brand dither, across the whole lower cell edge to edge; the longest visual goes in the tall lead cell and the widest in the wide cell; on tablet and phone every cell has the same height. Never replace an accepted bento layout with a "systemised" fixed grid without diffing it against the accepted one.
why: Founder on Kaching round 2: "not in a rectangular grey box", "this bento was clean, neat, consistent when scaling down, on mobile all the same heights, and now you messed it up everywhere", "we had the long visual, so put it first and the calendar as the long one".
check: visual.left == copy.left per cell; gap copy->visual identical across cells; no stage background; tablet/phone cell heights equal.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Visuals inside dark sections are dark visuals (dark panels with a faint white ring, light text, accent only on the selected/primary element). Never drop a bright white UI window onto a black band.
why: Founder on the Kaching migration section: "dark sections should have dark visuals, what's going on?"
applies: any product visual on a dark surface.
check: in dark sections, no visual panel has a background lighter than ~#2A2A2A.
origin: founder

text: [founder] When a founder-approved visual already exists (a motion artist's scene, a shipped section), revise it app by app: keep its composition, polish styling and motion, check it side by side against the original, and only then move to the next. Never regenerate a whole set in parallel from a new system; it drifts ("what you replaced is a bit shit", "let's go one by one").
check: each revised visual has a side-by-side with its original in the report.
origin: founder

text: [founder] A new brief gets a new design family, not the house style re-skinned: before building, change the layout family, alignment, nav grammar, button material, type voice and signature texture together (pick from `knowledge/web/light-hero-grammars.md`, `nav-grammars.md`, `button-grammars.md`, `type-voices.md`), research live references first (X designers, Godly, paper.design, the engine benchmarks), and when asked for a hero ship only the hero. Kestrel's centred Inter + grey pill nav + ink pill + rails/dot grid + framed dashboard is one family; repeating it for a new brand is a reject even at full polish.
why: Founder on Quorum v1 (2026-10-15), a Kestrel-grammar light hero plus a full page: "do something uniquer... not so alike with my past designs... this fuckign identical in style and everythign to other one we got... create something new with different layouts textures, maybe shaders, buttons effects nicer", "AND JUST THE HERO, not entire fucking page", "you have entire UI pedia... research deeper... look at X for other designers work combine do something amazing".
applies: every new hero or landing brief.
check: DIRECTION.md lists the six axes and how each differs from the last three builds; `ledger.mjs similar` passes; deliverable scope matches the ask.
origin: founder

text: [founder] For a fictional brand's logo, take an abstract mark from Pinterest and trace it (skill `logo-from-image`, `tools/trace_logo.mjs`) instead of drawing one; the founder swaps it if he dislikes it. Not Logoipsum.
why: Founder: "find an abstract logo from pinterest as image and convert it to svg and use as logo... instead of creating yourself", then "nouuu not logoipsum but take from pinterest"; on the pick: "nice logo pick".
check: `work/<name>/brand/ref/SOURCE.txt` exists and the trace sheet matches at 16px.
origin: founder

text: [founder] A hero's signature visual is product UI on an art surface, not loose stickers. Build one crisp, straight product window (a real control such as a waveform scrubber with tagged ranges and a playhead, real content, a side list) sitting on a fine art panel: an engraving or etching shader in one ink, light and fine (stroke period about 3px, ink about 70% alpha, never op-art black). Add at most one floating element, and it says what the product is doing right now (a status bar). Never use tilted sheets, scattered timestamp chips or chunky halftone colour blocks. (Nav dots in tag colours were "kinda cool" once, then rejected in v4: "no dots nearby the nav bar".)
why: Founder on Quorum v2 (halftone waveform with big tag-colour blocks, a tilted sheet, an insight card and three flag chips): "not bad for trying actually, but it ain't professional enough, especially the visual or the little three cards... the top nav bar with circles kinda cool... the visual needs improving".
check: one product window plus at most one floater; no rotated UI; the art panel has no saturated colour blocks; side-by-side with `knowledge/benchmarks/x-refs/aakib-1-v.jpg` and `split-heroes/lightfield-1440.png`.
origin: founder

text: [founder] When the founder says "clean, modern, simple, Marcel/Basit style", strip the hero to Marcel Kargul's Altrina grammar. Use a white page with one inset light panel (#f3f4f5, r20, 16px from the edges) and one fine-line art piece across its top: hairline strands that tell the product's story, with at most one accent colour and two or three small label chips on elbow leaders. Set the headline bottom-left at regular weight (Inter display 500, 84px, -0.045em), and put the subtitle and two square-ish buttons (r12, 48px; flat ink with a 1px top light, and white with a hairline ring) bottom-right on the art's focal axis. Do not add product windows, textures, grain, tilted cards or chips around the copy.
why: Founder on Quorum v3 (an engraved landscape behind an interview window): "I don't like it, I said do completely different stuff bro... clean modern simple, marcel, basit style more".
applies: heroes where the founder asks for clean or simple.
check: at most three things in the panel (art, headline, CTA block); one accent; side-by-side with `knowledge/benchmarks/kargul-deep/gallery/altrina-01.jpg`.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Line art must read as one coherent object. Use a ribbon of parallel hairlines (one centre curve, a width envelope, a twist) with 3D shading (strand alpha follows sin(twist), about 0.06-0.42), plus a fainter echo sheet behind. Never a tangle of independent random-phase strands; that reads as a scribble. Keep nav links plain: no coloured dots beside them.
why: Founder on Quorum v4 (a ribbon of 72 random-phase strands, a nav with tag-colour dots): "cool idea... ass visual and execution... no dots nearby the nav bar".
applies: generative line art and nav links.
check: strands never cross outside the twist points; one silhouette is readable at thumbnail size; nav links have no decorative markers.
origin: founder

text: [founder] The hero must say what the product is in one glance. If the visual needs explaining (abstract ribbons, sound landscapes, metaphors), it fails. The default for "clean SaaS" is the Lightfield split: - a plain light canvas (#f6f6f7); - copy on the left: Inter display 52/500/-0.04em Title Case h1, a two-line subtitle, an ink button and a grey button at r10; - the real app's core screen on the right, bleeding off the right and bottom edges. For Quorum that's the Insights table: ranked answers with mention strength, tag, sources and status; - one agent bar above the app showing it working; - at most one small "New" link bottom-left.
why: Founder on Quorum v4.1 (a twisted line-art ribbon through the logo): "the visual ass. like wtf even is this hero??? what it's about.. just design a SaaS product as clean as you can please".
check: a stranger can name the product category from the fold in 3 seconds; the visual is product UI, not illustration.
origin: founder

text: [founder] "Clean" never means bare. A clean SaaS split still needs: - a framed stage behind the product (an inset r24 panel with a rendered grain light field in one hue family, lit from a corner); - the product at Kargul detail density: a white active nav item, counts, a one-card summary strip with hairline cells, column-header icons, a selected row with a checked box, tinted tag chips, tinted-initial avatars, mention bars; - one peek card straddling the stage edge that proves the claim (the source quote and its clip); - tactile buttons (a gradient ink body with a top light and a crisp rim, and a raised white secondary), not flat fills; - quiet substance under the CTAs: a real product element such as an Ask box (three icon-tile bullet rows were rejected in v6).
why: Founder on Quorum v5 (plain grey canvas, a flat table, flat black/grey buttons): "good idea... just too simple and bad executed from buttons to colors and then bg... too empty... the product itself everything a bit just better done".
check: no flat-filled buttons; the stage has a rendered field; the product shows at least five of the Kargul micro-details; empty canvas under 35% of the copy column.
origin: founder

text: [founder] On a split hero, line the product stage up with the copy and fill the product to the edge: - the stage's top sits about 40px above the h1's cap line, and the stage bleeds off the bottom; - the copy block is centred against the visible stage; - tables and lists run full to the bleed with no fade-to-white; - fill space under the CTAs with a real product element (an Ask/composer box typing a question, with suggestion chips), never a stack of icon + text bullet points.
why: Founder on Quorum v6 ("ouuu this is cool"): "the right box is a bit up and then the left side looks strange... the bottom right corner just white... need the full list in the dashboard... those 3 points below... do some sort of visual or box but not like that".
check: no rows fade before the viewport edge; nothing under the CTAs is a bullet list; the stage top is within 60px of the h1 top.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Don't stack floaters over the product: a popover with its own visual (waveform, chart) on top of a dense dashboard competes with it, so cut it. Above the product, use one minimal live element: a status bar as a small toast stack (two ghost cards behind the front one, the front message cycling every ~2.6s). The composer under the CTAs earns its place by acting (the question types itself, then the chips swap for an "Answering from N quotes" line with source avatars), with a gradient hairline edge (accent to neutral to warm).
why: Founder on Quorum v6.1: "the title needs to be more up and the visual a bit higher or cooler... that little popover box with a voice visual... is too much and just interferes... above the dashboard something cooler with that line or stack, something more there minimally".
check: at most one floating element over the product; the h1 top sits at about 200-210 on a 900 fold.
origin: founder

text: [founder] A minimal live element above a product beats a stack. Use one status bar, plus a row of 44px square tiles to its right: the inputs feeding it, such as tinted-initial participant tiles, one with a green live dot, and a +N tile. Never ghost cards stacked behind. The composer under the hero CTAs should be big enough to carry a moment: about 64px below the CTAs and 470px wide, with a 17/550 question, and once typed it streams a one-sentence answer with the key finding highlighted in its tag colour and three citation chips (avatar plus timestamp). The founder loved the grain stage (Paper GrainGradient, corners shape, indigo/lavender/peach).
why: Founder on Quorum v6.2: "love the grain thingy... the thing above, I meant add maybe squares to the right or something minimal, not stack up... the below left side visual to be higher and have a bigger gap... better styled or a bit bigger... something cooler".
check: no stacked ghost cards; the composer shows a real answer with sources in the final frame.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Vertical rhythm on the copy side: the gap from the CTAs to the element below them equals the gap from that element to the fold (Quorum v6.5: 96 / 97px). Above the product, keep only the single status bar (no avatar rows, no stacks). Keep the gradient stage but drop only its grain texture (founder: "get rid only of the texture, not the bg": removing the whole gradient was wrong). Paper GrainGradient dithers at its colour edges even at noise 0, so render it at noise 0 and blur the shader layer (filter blur 26px, inset -40px so the edges stay full). The product dissolves into the stage: mask the window bottom (#000 62% to transparent 92%) and right (78% to 99%), with a short progressive blur (a 140px band of stacked 2/4/8px backdrop blurs; 230px "lasts too long").
why: Founder on Quorum v6.4: "move entire left side a tiny bit down so the gap for the visual and buttons is the same to the visual's bottom... remove the pfps, keep the initial version of the dashboard top... remove the grain bg and a slight blur out of the bottom of the dashboard or sides".
check: measure both gaps (within 4px); the product has no hard bottom edge inside the fold.
origin: founder

text: [founder] When the hero carries strong buttons, the nav CTAs must not repeat them: put "Sign in" as grey text and "Start free →" as ink text (underline draws in on hover, arrow nudges 2px), no filled nav buttons. When a floating element is removed from a product stage, close the gap in the same edit: re-inset the product to the stage's own side inset (44px) and grow it to fill. Never leave the hole and ask.
why: Founder on Quorum (2026-10-15), after the status card was removed and the window left at its old top: "maybe the nav bar CTAs to be different, like text, something different than now, and why didn't you move the dashboard up for the empty space to cover it???"
check: after removing an element, no gap larger than the surrounding insets remains; the nav CTA style differs from the hero CTA style.
origin: founder

text: [founder] An app sidebar follows Attio: one refined outline icon family (Phosphor regular, 16px, grey #7c7f85; the active row's icon goes fill), record types as 16px solid colour tiles (radius 4.5) with a white filled glyph, and enough real pages to feel like a product (workspace pages, Favorites, Records, Lists, Agents), grouped under small sentence-case headers. The whole nav fits a 1440x900 viewport without a clipped group; secondary actions (invite, help, settings) collapse into icon buttons in the user footer. White buttons get a crisp 1px ring plus a soft 1-2px lift (`.btn-white`), never a blurred halo.
why: Founder on Acquisity v3 (renamed Ferry): "not bad actually, you're getting better... I'd just improve the sidebar and the white buttons a tiny bit.. the sidebar icons look trash... overall sidebar itself should look more like attio and have more pages".
applies: SaaS app UI and hero dashboards.
check: one icon library in the sidebar; record tiles solid with white glyphs; no group cut at 900px tall; white button shadow = 0 0 0 1px ring + <= 2px blur lift.
origin: founder

text: [founder] The last 5% to Marcel/Rico level is tiny effects plus consistency, so finish every product screen with this pass: one icon family across sidebar and canvas (state = fill weight, never a second library); one card-header grammar everywhere (16px solid tile + white glyph, 14/600 title, soft meta, actions right, same 48px band); micro-visuals that carry data (KPI micro-bar sparks with the latest period in the accent, segmented meters for rates, dotted underline on metric labels); charts compare against something (previous period dotted grey under a 1.5px accent line, monotone smoothing that never overshoots a real value, dashed gridlines, a hover crosshair + tooltip, an end-point dot); only one attribute per row is a filled chip, other statuses are icon + text; table edge cells share the card's 16px inset; dense cells use compact values ("12m", "1d") so nothing clips.
why: Founder on Ferry: "we're so close but not marcel or rico quality by a tiny bit, which comes down to tiny effects and consistencies"; while studying Rico's analytics, Attio's charts and Kargul's CRM: "you're looking at fire examples tho".
check: icon libraries imported in the product = 1; every card header renders through one component; each chart has a comparison series and a hover state; filled chips per table row <= 1; no clipped cell text at 1440 wide.
origin: founder

text: [founder] A split product hero stays clean: plain canvas behind the copy (Lightfield, Attio), the copy block vertically centred and the product doing the visual work. The copy side still needs quiet substance (founder round 3: "titles subtitle and buttons and that's all??? ... too empty"): one row of three stats under the CTAs (big display number + one-line soft label, hairline dividers, product specs not invented results) and a minimal texture such as the fine dot grid, cleared behind the type and stopping before the product stage. If the hero needs art, confine it to one stage panel directly behind the product (Folk's grain gradient, Cursor's painting, Granola's collage); never a full-page pattern, contour field or scattered decorative numbers, and never a "how it works" step list in the hero.
why: Founder on the Ferry hero: kept "the title subtitle buttons nav bar the product nice", rejected the live sea-chart contour background and the three lit-up steps: "BG WITH THOSE LIKE THREE STEPS LIKE WTF IS SO STUPID... find better cleaner examples of this and do it better".
check: no busy pattern (contours, scattered numbers, step lists) anywhere; copy side = headline, subtitle, CTAs, one stats row, optional dot grid faded behind the type; at most one floating surface over the product.
source: founder, Ferry hero round 1, 2026-10-09; knowledge/benchmarks/split-heroes/lightfield-1440.png, folk-1440.png, attio-1440.png, product-heroes/cursor-1440.png
origin: founder

text: [founder] A product hero must feel alive and show enough of the product: render the dashboard at hero scale (about 0.8 zoom, ~11-12px text) so sidebar, KPIs and a full table read at once, and let the story play inside the product (rows arrive, AI states change, a cursor acts inline, numbers tick) with at most one narrating chip above the window (Lightfield's agent pill). No pop-up cards floating over the copy side; a static 1:1 crop of one table reads "empty... too simple". A soft blue stage panel behind the product was "not bad".
why: Founder on Ferry hero round 2: "the bluish not bad just idk about second card like popping up nor the size of the dashboard... it's just empty and no stuff going on, it's not good... too simple".
check: something in the product changes at least every ~1-1.5s for the first ~10s; visible product shows the sidebar, KPIs and >= 8 table rows; no floating card overlaps the copy column.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Hero products build in fully and in order, and numbers roll: after the frame lands, every part of the product enters on a top-to-bottom stagger (sidebar items, header, tabs, KPI cards, table rows), and every number rolls up digit by digit in its own slot (kit `RollingNumber`), never a plain fade or a whole-number count. The live story starts only after the build completes.
why: Founder on Ferry hero round 4: "product should like load in with stagger and fully load in plus like the numbers to count up professionally by sliding up each number... more professional".
applies: product heroes and product visuals in sections.
check: filmstrip at 0.3/0.7/1.0/1.4s shows frame, then staggered contents; KPI digits roll; nothing in the product is static from frame 1.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Dark heroes must be premium dark (Linear, Vercel, Raycast grade), never "dev-tool template" dark: no neo-brutalist hard offset-block buttons, no muddy coloured glow on graphite, no flat dark product slab that sinks into the canvas, no random pastel data colours, no heavy 700 headline with crushed tracking. The product window in dark needs light: a defined edge (1px top highlight + hairline ring), a surface step above the canvas, and one controlled key light; data colours come from one tuned ramp. The split band layout (headline left, subtitle + CTAs right on the headline baseline, full-width product below) is good and reusable.
why: Founder on Tracewell (V1 dark hero #1): "straight up dogshit"; "the app and the buttons and everything else about it (except layout, I know that layout is good to use)... those buttons... looking ass and in general the dark design of the SaaS ass as well".
applies: every dark hero and dark product UI.
check: side-by-side with knowledge/benchmarks/dark/linear and vercel folds via tools/compare.mjs before delivery; product window luminance step >= 4% above canvas with a visible top edge; buttons from knowledge/web/button-grammars.md dark recipes, not offset blocks.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Florian Hoeller (@flohoeller; affectui.com, adfects.com) is the top quality bar for product UI, components and light SaaS heroes, alongside Kargul, Rico and Attio. Study his work before building those: calm Inter 500 headlines at modest size (46-52px, about -0.03em), muted #666-#737373 copy, a dark pill built from two stacked gradients with a 1px ring plus a 4% grey ghost twin, card-in-card showcase frames (r24 outer, r18 grey inner stage), believable content in every pixel (real-feeling names, numbers, sources), product states that move (thinking timers, steps landing one by one, morphs into success), and his depth-of-field collage hero (tilted UI fragments at different blur depths around a clean centre).
why: Founder: "STUDY THIS GUY FULLY I WANT HIS QUALITY EVERYTHING LIKE HIM... HE'S THE BEST".
applies: components, product UI, light SaaS heroes.
check: compare against knowledge/benchmarks/flohoeller/*.png with tools/compare.mjs; read knowledge/web/flohoeller-craft.md.
origin: founder

text: [founder] In a minimal (Flo Hoeller) hero, the composition must be calm and balanced: one clear focal object, symmetric or deliberately weighted supporting pieces, consistent tilt direction and focus logic, lots of white. A scattered collage of UI fragments with mixed tilts, random blur and one big sharp card off to the side reads "badly designed for this minimalism". Prefer the product moment as the centred focal object with a few ghosted siblings behind it, or his very faint, evenly distributed collage.
why: Founder on Tandem hero v1: "hero is a bit like badly designed idk for this minimalism"; same round: approval request and product "kinda cool".
check: fragments mirror across the centre axis (or follow one stated diagonal); at most one sharp focal object, centred; every other fragment shares one blur/opacity step per depth.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Product UI icons: use Lucide (stroke 1.5-1.75 at 16px) for app chrome unless the build says otherwise; and place things properly: one left edge for icons, one for labels, counts in one right column, section labels aligned to item text, no orphan icon lines.
why: Founder on Tandem product: "product just use lucide icons and just better sidebar and properly placed stuff".
check: one icon library imported in the product; sidebar icon x and label x identical across rows; counts right-aligned to one x.
origin: founder

text: [founder] The top of a product sidebar is quiet and clean: one workspace tile (a solid rounded square with a letter or glyph, padded, never a clipped or overlapping mark at the edge), the workspace name, a chevron, a collapse icon; under it at most one light search field (white, hairline ring, kbd hint). The primary "New" action is a normal nav row or a ghost button, never a heavy dark pill with a kbd chip crammed into the sidebar.
why: Founder on Tandem product round 2: "sidebar top wtf???" (crop: clipped two-square logo, heavy dark "New run" pill with an N kbd, separate search square).
check: the workspace mark is fully inside the sidebar with >= 8px inset; no dark filled button in the sidebar; search and rows share one left edge.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Depth-of-field side cards fall off gently: each depth step loses little. Near siblings stay almost sharp (blur <= 0.6px, opacity >= 0.85); the far ones stay legible (blur <= 1.2px, opacity >= 0.7). The fade comes from the white edge mask and the tilt, not from heavy blur.
why: Founder on Tandem hero round 2: "the ones to the sides blur out too fast" (they were 1.5px/0.7 and 6px/0.32).
applies: heroes with ghost or collage cards.
check: computed filter blur and opacity per depth match the caps above.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Side and ghost cards in a hero are real, designed mini-components, never filler: each one shows a different kind of UI (a chart with real bars, a list with avatars, switches, a step log with app tiles), built in the same anatomy as the focal card (Flo's grey tray with a status strip holding a white card), with matched heights per depth pair and coherent sample content from the same story. No empty gradient bars, no lone big number, no plain text lists.
why: Founder on Tandem hero round 3: "the hero visuals form the very sides are too noob and in general should be better designed and showcases like not bad now just like do it better" (crop: far-left "312h" card with an empty gradient bar, far-right three-line inbox, near cards as plain text lists).
applies: heroes with side, ghost or collage cards.
check: every side card contains at least one non-text UI element (chart, switch, avatar, tile, progress); the mirrored pair share one height; no element is a placeholder shape.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Component posts (the X / social format) follow Flo: one component alone on the #fafafa preview canvas, scaled up (~1.5x) inside its grey tray, the tray strip narrating the state, and a real cursor (Lucide MousePointer2) that travels, presses and lets go in sync with the component's own phases. Record the full loop at 4K60 plus an X-preset upload.
why: Founder: "get me a high quality of the approval request component just like he does on X and animate it too".
check: cursor target measured after the entrance settles; one full state loop inside the clip.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Present logos the way studios do before asking for a verdict: each finalist on white, on the brand colour and on ink, at 32/24/16 px, in the real nav lockup (mark 1.43x cap height, gap 0.28x mark, wordmark >= 20px), with its one-sentence idea; then drop the chosen mark into the live build (nav, favicon, the agent avatar) so it is judged in place, never only on a white artboard.
why: Founder: "the logo is the last piece that's still shitty". The references (logosystem.co, svgl.app) show marks on brand fields and in lockups; a mark judged alone at 256px hides every small-size and pairing failure.
check: work/<name>/brand/present.png exists for the shipped mark; the build uses the mark in nav and product.
origin: founder

text: [founder] A logo built only from textbook primitives (a disc with slits, two half discs, circles in a row) reads as a road sign or clip art, not a brand, even when it passes every measured check. Marks the founder will accept look drawn: custom curves with controlled tension, a distinctive silhouette, an optical refinement pass, and a presentation on a brand field the way studios show them (logosystem.co level). Passing logo_measure is the floor, never the evidence.
why: Founder on the Tandem T-cut and Halves finalists (constructed from primitives, 0 fails): "yeah it's pretty awful, continue on researching how logos are done".
check: put the finalist next to 6 logosystem.co references on the same brand field; if it looks like a pictogram or signage, it is not done.
origin: founder

text: [founder] A hero shows the product, not the whole product. Show one view at a readable size with fewer, larger elements (about 6-10 rows or items, one panel, one moment of AI), not a full multi-panel workspace with a thread, chart, approval, inspector and timeline at once. Unique structure is welcome, but the product density should match what shipped premium heroes show.
why: Founder on Halyard (Marcel grid + Rico workspace): "not bad for uniqueness... just yeah nobody shows that much or high product design", then asked for heroes "a bit more normal, like ours".
check: product window in the fold shows <= 3 regions (e.g. sidebar + one main view + one AI moment) and no text under 12.5px; count visible distinct components <= 12.

text: [founder] No "editorial luxury" SaaS heroes: a poster-size didone serif (Bodoni-class) over a brown warm-black field, a lamp vignette and a tilted paper document reads as a template for a law firm or a perfume, not a software product. Dark SaaS heroes stay in the polished modern grammar (Kestrel, Linear, Basit-level craft: grotesk display, crisp product UI, controlled light), and a "brand campaign" variant still needs a product-grade visual, not a beige sheet of paper.
why: Founder on Quillwork (hero B: Bodoni Moda 84px, #120e0a warm black, grain + lamp spotlight, a tilted contract sheet with tracked changes): "if this is what you're designing now - straight up dogshit". Same round, Weekline (Kestrel composition made dark) was not called out.
check: display face is not a didone/fashion serif unless the brief is luxury/editorial; the hero visual is product UI or an owned generative/graphic field, not a paper mockup; canvas is not a brown/sepia near-black.

text: [founder] Deliver heroes as screenshots by default; record videos only when asked.
why: Founder: "no videos tho, just screenshots get me".
check: no .mp4 in the delivery folder unless requested.

text: [founder] Hero subtitles run at most 2 lines and break properly: balanced lines (text-wrap: balance or a hand-set break), no orphan word on the last line, the max-width tuned to the copy, not a fixed 440-560px. If the copy needs 3 lines, cut the copy.
why: Founder on Murmur (subtitle ran 3 lines, last line "type up."): "for subtitle try to put proper text clipping to other line, max 2 lines".
check: subtitle height <= 2 x line-height; last line >= 40% of the first line's width.

text: [founder] The announcement pill above the headline is allowed but must not be the same template every time: pick from the pill variants in `system/variety/buttons-2/` (or design a custom one for the brand) and never reuse the last build's pill. The stock "[New] text →" capsule is the AI tell, not the idea of a pill.
why: Founder: "that top card above heading is optional cuz it's often considered AI", then clarified: "not off by default, just have more variants and more custom".
check: pill construction differs from the previous build's; it says something specific.

text: [founder] Buttons vary by their inner effect, not by their shape: keep the shape fully round (pill) or softly rounded with smooth corners (squircle-like, radius 12-18px at 44-52px tall); vary the clean effect inside (gloss, inner glow, gradient rim, rolling label, arrow tile, light sweep, spotlight, split segment, icon tile). Do not reuse the previous two builds' primary effect. Never go brutalist, square-cut or heavy offset-shadow.
why: Founder: "explore more button styles, so that all of our designs wouldn't be repetitive", then: "mostly fully round or like smoother corners, but the effects inside of them and stuff, just clean".
check: primary CTA radius is a pill or 12-18px smooth corner; its effect class differs from the last two builds (Murmur ice gloss, Weekline slide-swap). Catalogue: `system/variety/buttons-2/`.
origin: founder

text: [founder] When a button, row or card leads with a tile (icon square, app icon, avatar box), the tile's left inset equals its top and bottom insets, exactly. The tile's radius is concentric with the container (outer radius - inset) when there is room; otherwise it stays smaller than the outer radius. Size controls with `box-sizing: border-box` so padding never inflates the height and doubles the vertical inset.
why: Founder on the Buttons II app-tile button (left inset 6px, top/bottom 12px because padding was added on top of a fixed height): "WTF IS THE LEFT SPACING FOR THE CARD WITH RECTANGULAR BOX OR ICONS ON LEFT???? IT SHOULD BE SAME AS TOP AND BOTTOM PADDINGS". The new probe then found the same fault shipped in Halyard's bento lanes (10 left vs 8 top/bottom).
applies: all buttons, list rows, cards and chips with a leading tile.
check: `node tools/check.mjs` probe `shape.inset-tile` (FAIL): left = top = bottom within 1.5px, radius concentric.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Every rounded box uses Apple continuous corners (squircles): cards, windows, panels, inputs, menus, tiles, square-ish buttons. Capsules, circles and dots stay true round. Builds import `squircle.css` (in the kit template; copy `system/effects/squircle.css` into coss/Next apps and import it in globals.css), which sets `corner-shape: superellipse(1.32)` where supported and keeps the old border-radius elsewhere; author radii about 1.2x larger than a circular-arc radius so the visible curve stays the same size. Hero objects that must be squircle in every browser (app icons, device frames, the product window) use the SVG path from `squircle.ts`.
why: Founder: "could we create designs with apple soothing squircles always??? cuz like the way it makes everything look more premium".
check: `node tools/check.mjs` probe `shape.squircle` >= 90% of rounded non-capsule boxes.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Borders are learned, not defaulted: 1px rings at ink 6-10% (light) or white 6-12% (dark) drawn as box-shadow rings, one edge treatment per box, nested radius = outer - inset, padding inside < gap between < section gap, no dividers inside a card. Read `knowledge/web/borders-and-nesting.md` (BN-01..12, UI Pedia principles + measured numbers) before building product UI.
why: Founder: "have you learned about borders, like the gap between and then what border size to get that professionalism? ... apply in action and understand why from the book UI Pedia".
check: BN-01..12 checks; `shape.inset-tile`.
origin: founder

text: [founder] A divider inside a bordered card runs edge to edge: no transparent 1px border that stops the line 1-2px short of the visible ring.
why: Founder, 2026-10-12, Kaching Email card: "the bottom border of that not full width like 2px spacing from sides wtf".
check: divider left/right offset from the card's visible edge = 0.
origin: founder

text: [founder] A wide visual box is a brief for a wide, cinematic composition: use the full width with a left-to-right story built from real product UI fragments and real brand marks (the client's logo, real app icons, real assistant marks). Never a small centred node-and-line diagram floating in a big empty box. Before building any non-trivial visual, research 8+ real references and show 2-3 concept stills for a pick before animating.
why: Founder, 2026-10-12, Kaching MCP "Connect once. Ask away." v1 (busy node diagram, dither blob instead of the logo): "looks a bit ugly... we have a logo bro... just not busy, just simple and quality... not AI shit". v2 (calm centred column in a wide box): "this visual is super shit bro... we have a long visual for a reason to have something cooler, way smoother and just better in all ways... did you use larpo engine or find any examples online?".
check: the visual's content spans >= 80% of its box width at desktop; references and concept stills exist before the animation is built.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Busy is a defect: at most one moving element at a time in a looping section visual, no box-in-box-in-box, no redundant labels, and app/brand colour only on the brand's own marks and data.
why: Founder, 2026-10-12, on the Kaching MCP connection v1: "in general just not busy just simple and quality and using our styles colors and ideology not to be AI shit".
check: count simultaneously animating elements per frame; nesting depth of bordered containers <= 2.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Product UI must read clean: one accent at most (ink is the default accent), colour only where it carries meaning (late = red, needs action = one warm dot), monochrome vendor logos and neutral monogram tiles, avatars on a neutral ground, and no more than one surface step (page + cards, or sidebar + page, never canvas + panel + cards). Separate with space before edges: count the ringed boxes in the fold and cut every ring that a gap could replace (checkboxes appear on hover, row actions are ghost, keycaps only on the search field).
why: Founder on Settle v1 (Kargul-style dense AP dashboard, 0 check fails): "with those colors and layouts it's looking a bit dirty you know... I'm not a fan of this style... I think you could do better and cleaner". Measured in that fold: 5 accent hue families plus coloured logos, faces and monograms, 55 ringed boxes, 3 surface layers on a warm grey canvas.
applies: product UI, dashboards, app screens in heroes.
check: fold census: <= 2 accent hue families (excluding photos), ringed boxes <= ~25 at 1440x900, surface fills <= 2, canvas neutral (chroma < 0.01).
origin: founder

text: [founder] Product frames sit straight-on at rest: no perspective tilt (rotateX/rotateY) on a laptop, browser or app window in the hero. A tilt may only be used as an entrance that settles to 0°. Dragged or floating objects inside the product tilt at most 1-2°.
why: Founder on Perch v1 (MacBook display at rotateX 15°, sides slanting inward ~45px across the fold): "the visual representation is a bit tilted and off bro wtf fix that".
applies: all product heroes; overrides the variety picker's `tilted-3d` layout (read it as "3D entrance, flat rest").
check: computed transform of the product frame at rest is identity (no rotateX/Y); left and right edges are vertical in the fold screenshot.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Interaction moments inside a product visual (drag, drop, select, hover) are drawn in the platform's native grammar and polished to the same level as the visual itself: the drag image is the real item (a thumbnail of the actual content, opaque, soft lift shadow, a small copy badge, the cursor gripping its lower edge), the source slot dims, and the target shows a native indicator (an insertion line between paragraphs, a highlighted row), never a dashed placeholder box with "Drop here" text or a dark UI card dragged across a light app. Windows the moment lands in are fully visible and carry real content, not half-hidden under another layer.
why: Founder on Perch v1 (a dark shelf card with a big green badge dragged into a pink dashed "Drop to insert image" box in a near-empty, half-covered window): "where in the visual the mouse drags sth box is stupidly designed as well as what's going on in the visual, that should be more polished as the visual itself".
applies: product heroes and product visuals with a demonstrated action.
check: crop the moment at 2x: would it pass as a real macOS/iOS/web screenshot? No dashed drop boxes, no placeholder copy, no overlapping half-hidden windows.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Give the hero headline room before anything else: when the fold is tight, drop the announcement pill first, then tighten the product's position; never squeeze the title. The subtitle is set by hand into two phrase-lines (break at a phrase boundary, each line 32-45 characters, near-equal length), and it is short: cut words before letting it wrap.
why: Founder on Perch round 2: "a bit too tight the title and stuff, if stuff doesn't fit then no top bar, and the subtitle looks badly formatted and a bit too long. I'm trying to get that nice clipping to the other line as I've taught you".
check: subtitle = 2 lines with an explicit break, line lengths within 15% of each other; headline top >= 120px below the nav on a 900px fold.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Product visuals use real images: actual screenshots (our own builds are fair game), photos with clear rights, real link previews; never grey bars standing in for an image. When no rights-cleared photo exists, ask the founder before downloading or generating (credits).
why: Founder on Perch round 2: "use real images or something in the visual".
check: every image slot in the fold renders a raster image or a real UI capture.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Deliver hero rounds as choices: at least 3 layouts and 4-5 display fonts on one switchable build (`?layout=`, `?font=`), plus a labelled contact sheet, so the founder picks instead of reacting to one take.
why: Founder on Perch round 2: "provide more font variants and layout runs so I could choose which is best".
check: delivery includes contact-sheet.png and the URL params.

text: [founder] A reference image sent for one thing (a logo) changes only that thing. Never restyle the palette, page ground or wallpaper from it unless asked, and never touch an approved look while applying unrelated fixes.
why: Founder on Perch round 3, where the green palette was taken from his logo reference: "nouuu not green bro, the other design was better and all you did now is ass". Round 2 (Apple-light #f5f5f7 page, warm orange wallpaper) was restored, keeping only the fixes he had asked for.

text: [founder] Premium dark dashboards are neutral, not blue: graphite surfaces (no blue-tinted canvas or periwinkle everywhere); colour is reserved for state, and the polish comes from material (tactile surfaces, inner highlights, soft glows on data) rather than hue. Maps and signature visuals get the same finish as the product: fine dense dots with edge fade, crisp nodes with soft light, chip labels, an animated flow, never a sparse grid of flat dots.
why: Founder on Kite v1 (blue-black recipe, periwinkle accent, 6px flat dot map): "not bad, just the map is not polished, plus don't do it so blue please, do the map better and effects better, everything more polished and premium, Marcel / Rico style".
check: canvas and surfaces chroma < 0.01; accent pixels <= 2% of the fold; map dot pitch <= 5px with a radial edge fade.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Dashboard and hero load-ins settle in about 2.5 seconds: not 4 ("faster"), not 1.8 ("too fast and not smooth"). One expo-out curve (0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) everywhere, durations 0.6-1.2s that overlap, staggers 35-60ms, glides instead of bouncy springs, no blur on large surfaces. Heavy setup work (dot maps, geo tests) must never block the main thread at load: test land with a canvas mask, not per-dot polygon tests.
why: Founder on Kite: v1 load-in (~3.8s) "FASTER"; v2 (~1.8s, springs, blur on cards) "too fast and not smooth". Measured: ~60k geoContains calls blocked the page for seconds and froze the load-in in a fresh browser.
applies: every animated product hero and dashboard.
check: the last element settles at 2.2-2.8s; the first frame after load paints within ~50ms (rAF probe).
origin: founder

text: [founder] Hero backgrounds stay minimal: a faint dot grid fading from the centre, fine grain, hairline rails and rules with small + marks where they cross. No big 3D objects (a rising dot-matrix globe was "even worse") and no busy texture. The product must show enough in the fold: frame top at or above ~510px on a 900px fold (64px under the CTAs), so the KPIs and the signature visual are visible.
why: Founder on the Kite landing: v1 faint dot-map texture: "we need better bg"; v2 rotating globe horizon: "even worse... do something simple, with borders or textures, minimal and cool"; plus "show enough of the product itself".
check: product frame top <= 520px at 1440x900; background effects <= 2 layers, no canvas scene behind the hero.
origin: founder

text: [founder] A landing page for a dark product uses the product's own material, not a generic dark template: the nav as the product's recessed segmented track with a raised active tile, tactile chips and buttons with the product's bevels, a solid near-white headline at 500 (second line softer), one soft overhead beam lighting the product frame, and a tactile bezel that catches that light (gradient, 1px dark ring, bright top edge).
why: Founder on the Kite landing (minimal grid hero): "better, but not premium enough for our dashboard-like style".
check: nav, chip, CTAs and product frame reuse the product's shadow/gradient tokens; exactly one light source in the hero.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Build exactly the scope asked for. "Build a cool landing page" after a hero round means the hero (one 1440x900 fold), not a full multi-section site; add sections only when they are named.
why: Founder on the Kite landing (full page with bento, steps, CTA, footer): "just hero bro, not entire web".
check: the deliverable's sections match the words in the request.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Less is more on dark heroes: no glows at all (no overhead beams, halos around the product, light streaks on bezels, glows under buttons), no background texture, no decorative rules. A flat near-black page, the type, two buttons and the product in a plain frame (1px light ring, faint top highlight, dark drop). Polish lives in the type and the product, not in effects.
why: Founder on the Kite hero with overhead beam, lit bezel, dot grid and rules: "still not premium, especially the glows and stuff wtf" then "less is more".
check: zero radial gradients or white box-shadow blurs outside the product UI; background is one flat colour.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Between "too much" and "too little": hero headline about 52px at weight 500 (not 66-80px), no announcement chip by default (it has become our repeated tell), and one quiet structural background: hairline rails/rules with small square marks, diagonal hatching confined to the side gutters, or a fine square grid fading out downward. Structure, not light. Deliver these as switchable variants.
why: Founder on the bare Kite hero: "now too little... the title is a bit drastic and big, and that indicator above the title, let's remove it, it's too repetitive in our designs... we need some textures or borders in the bg, or try different layouts".
check: h1 <= 56px; no chip unless asked; background = one hairline/texture layer at <= 7% white, zero glows.

text: [founder] Hero titles are short and specific, 3-5 words with an idea in them ("Latency Has An Address."), never a long category description ("The Edge Network That Tells You Why." was "too shallow and just long"). Background structure is wide-spaced (120px grid cells, kept around the copy, away from the product), never dense patterns close to the content. The product dissolves into the page at the fold with a short fade + light blur (~150px), never a hard cut and never eating the signature visual.
why: Founder on the Kite hero variants: "layout good - copy ass, the title too shallow and just long, and bg a bit stupid and too close, and no bottom blur or something".
check: h1 <= 5 words; background cell size >= 100px and masked off the product; bottom fade 120-180px.

text: [founder] Product flows inside an existing app (Sellify Video Ad Creator, 2026-10-14) use ONE container grammar on every screen: a grey tray (radius 20, 4px inset, ring) with its title strip on the grey (plain 16px secondary icon + title + soft meta + action right; never a black icon tile), white cards inside (radius 16, 1px ink-alpha ring, no shadow), secondary info and actions on a tray footer strip; fields inside white cards use the app's own grey "work" input surface via the component's prop (never white inputs on white, never `!important` overrides); type only from the app's tuned scale (Geist 12/14/18 at 450/500, the app's letter-spacing tokens, no 13px/600 off-scale sizes); video media is 9:16 in galleries and the preview, but list-row thumbnails are square crops (a narrow 9:16 sliver reads as a capsule); status is an outlined chip with a coloured dot, never a coloured icon tile or check badge.
why: Founder on rounds 1-4: "out of place not nice nor consistent", "wtf is with aspect ratios", "those little black icon boxes don't look good enough nor geist... configured good enough", "white bg then gray input box... like we have in our design language", "entire flow, containers everything properly consistently built". Reference: affectUI blocks (knowledge/benchmarks/flohoeller/affectui-blocks-*).
applies: product UI built inside a client app.
check: every section renders through one panel component; zero white inputs inside white cards; font sizes in the flow ⊆ the app scale; no row thumbnail narrower than 9:16 at < 64px wide.

text: [founder] When a hero keeps missing, stop iterating blind: pick a measured reference (knowledge/benchmarks/dark/*.measure.json + fold png) and replicate its grammar exactly (positions, type tuple, nav, frame), then swap in our content and judge with `tools/compare.mjs` side by side. For dark product heroes the default reference is Linear: 73px nav + full-width 8% hairline, 1280 container, left-aligned 64/64 Inter 510 -1.4px #f7f8f8 headline at y=277, one muted subtitle line at y=445 with a quiet "New → link" right, no hero buttons, product frame #0f1011 + 8% hairline r12 at y=530 bleeding off the fold.
why: Founder after six Kite hero rounds (glows, globe, textures, chips, centred stacks): "so bad now I have no words bro... find some example online and replicate".
check: compare.mjs side-by-side saved in the work folder; headline/subtitle/frame tops within 10px of the reference.
origin: founder

text: [founder] A dark hero needs exactly one strong, tasteful visual moment, or it reads "flat and empty"; glows scattered around ("wtf") and bare black ("too little") both fail. Use Basit's cinematic grammar: an inset framed stage (r28, 14px from the viewport), one rendered light field kept SOFT: a wide, blurred, low-contrast sheen (peak alpha <= ~0.08, blur >= 60px, light grain), neutral silver with a faint warm cast, never a thin bright streak or laser line (founder: "be careful with bg elements, now it looks cheap and ugly") whose brightest band crests just behind the product's top edge and falls to black before the copy, a floating glass capsule nav, a centred 60px / 450 / -0.05em two-line headline with the second line at ~50% value, 16px sub-copy close under it, 48px CTAs (white lit from inside + glass), and the product ~72% wide in a glass frame dissolving at the bottom.
why: Founder after the Linear replica: "it's flat and empty... what didn't [work] is everything from font styling to layout and colors and effects... you cooked with the dashboard, best thing in the world". Murmur (same grammar) was accepted.
check: one light source rendered (canvas/image), not CSS blobs; light luminance under the h1/CTAs < 8%; product top in the brightest band.
origin: founder

text: [founder] What the founder loves in our light builds (Kestrel) is type, lightness, spacing and professionalism, not effects; carry exactly that into dark. Default dark product hero = Supabase top half + Cursor product stage: full-width hairline nav (links left after the logo, Sign in outline + light CTA right), 1200 container, a calm two-line 56px / 500 / -0.035em Inter headline on the left (second line soft grey), the description in a right column (17/27, ~420px), compact 40px CTAs, then a full-width stage panel (#111113, hairline, faint 18px dot grid) with the product window floating inside it. The founder named Cursor and Supabase as the heroes he likes.
why: Founder: "look at the light designs I've loved, the way you did the font, lightness, spacing and professionalism... I like Cursor, Supabase".
check: no glow/light field; headline <= 60px at 500; product stage top <= 430px.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Dark hero type and controls, built properly: the headline is one colour (no grey second line), bold and tight (Inter 600, 60px, -0.04em, line-height 1.04, two short balanced lines); the subtitle is a real block (18/28, #a1a1a6, two hand-set lines under the headline); the hero buttons reuse the product's own button construction (white bevelled pill: #fff->#dedee0 gradient, 1px dark ring, inset white top; dark tactile pill), the same in the nav at 34px. Use the logo the founder supplies, traced to SVG, as mark + wordmark.

check: h1 one computed colour, weight >= 600; hero buttons share the product's button tokens.

text: [founder] Big Inter must be the display cut: import `@fontsource-variable/inter/opsz.css` (never plain `@fontsource-variable/inter`, which has no optical-size axis), set `font-optical-sizing: auto` and `font-feature-settings: "cv11","ss01"`, and use Kestrel's headline tuple (68-72px / 550 / -0.045em / 1.04). One family across the hero and the product inside it; never Inter outside and another grotesk inside the frame.

text: [founder] A hero background can borrow the product's own design elements (Kite: the dashboard's dot-matrix map, white nodes with soft light, chip labels, hairline routes), clearly visible (dots up to ~50% white, not a whisper: founder rejected a 40% calmer pass as "too minimal and stupid"), set low so it wraps around the copy, between the rails, cleared behind the copy by a mask and fading before the product; labels never touch the headline, subtitle or CTAs. The subtitle is two hand-set balanced lines (~600px measure), never one 1000px line.

text: [founder] Hero buttons are the product's own buttons scaled up, kept simple: full pills (rounded-full) like the dashboard's Deploy (white #fff->#dcdcde, 1px dark ring, inset white top) and its dark tactile pill; no arrow tiles, no extra bevel stacks, 44px.

text: [founder] When the founder says a past version "had it right", restore that exact styling and change only what he named (here: position). For the Kite background map that is the soft version: dots 0.10 + heat 0.34 (max 0.5), r 0.95, a long soft cut-out around the copy (radial 40% x 44%, transparent 64% -> black 100%), bottom fade from 78%, no comets. Nav for a dark product hero: plain text links right after the logo (15px / 500 / grey, 28px gaps), no track or button styling; logo mark 26px + 23px wordmark; nav CTA a small 36px pill.

text: [founder] Background product elements stay monochrome: no red state, pulses or extra chips in the hero backdrop (the story colour belongs inside the product); when the backdrop needs more presence, make the map bigger, not busier. Keep labels inside the rails.

text: [founder] Never stack a 1px outer ring and a 1px inset top highlight (or an inner ring) on the same dark box: at 1-2x they read as a double top border with a dark gap. Dark surfaces get ONE light ring (white 7-10%) plus soft drop shadows; tactile depth comes from the fill gradient, not extra edge lines (BN-04 enforced). Backdrop blur only works if the blurred element is not inside a masked/filtered layer: put glass chips on their own layer above the masked art.
