check: no box-shadow list on one element contains both `0 0 0 1px` and `inset 0 1px 0`; glass chips' parent has no mask-image/filter.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Inside an existing client app, every new screen (a new step, a new feature such as avatars) is built from that app's established component kit, never from a fresh stylesheet. For Sellify that kit is the Video Ad Creator studio: `StudioPanel` (grey tray, title strip, white card, footer strip), `StudioStatus`, the step tray, `.gallery` / `.tile9` / `.libraryCard` with 3:4 or 9:16 media, the segmented control, list rows, the sticky footer bar and the owner components (Button system sizes, Input/Textarea density default, Select/Popover/Dialog appearance system). A screen that invents its own tray, card, badge, step strip or choice tile reads as a different product even when each part is tidy.
why: Founder on the ENG-2105 guided set + avatars pass (own CSS module, 13px/600 type, filled badges, padded section boxes, bordered choice tiles): "what you designed right now is super super bad and incosistent and jsut the ugliest sheeet in the world... do it in our new after effects alignui style bro please cmon... just nice and sleek".
applies: product UI inside an existing app.
check: the new screen imports the app's kit (for Sellify `video-ad-studio.module.css` / `StudioPanel`); zero new tray/card/badge/stepper recipes; font sizes in the screen are within the app scale (12/14/18), weights within {450, 500}.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Design for content volume, not the happy-path sample: more items wrap into more rows (columns never shrink below ~200px and buttons never shrink or clip); names and meta cut off with an ellipsis (or clamp to 2 lines) and keep a title tooltip; long lists, option menus and popovers get a max-height (about 60dvh) with their own scroll; a row of cards keeps equal heights with actions pinned to the bottom; sticky bars never cover the last row (pad the scroll area by the bar height); test every grid with 1, 4, 12 and 40 items and every label with a 60-character string.
why: Founder: "have in mind that there may be a lot of ocntent pieces so make sure they woudl now squich... be prepared for that scroll bars or heights".
check: render fixtures at 1/4/12/40 items and a long-name item; no element narrower than its min width, no clipped button label, no text overflow, every scroll container has a max-height.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Final checks are part of the job, not optional: before any handoff measure computed styles across the whole flow (every text field, textarea, select trigger and custom picker trigger shares one height and one radius; one edge per box and per overlay; hover, selected and focus follow one language) and fix every mismatch before showing it. The founder should never be the one who finds a mismatched field.
why: Founder on the Video Ad Creator voice field (2026-10-14): "WHY THE INPUT FIELD ROUDNESS NOT THE SMAE AS OTHERS... WHY YOU KEEP ON MESSING SUTFF UP AND NOT DOING IFNAL CHECKS"; same rounds: dropdowns with double borders, an upload dialog not built from our components, and "especially on hover and selected like visuals ... just ass".
check: an audit script (Sellify: `studio.cjs AUDIT=1`) reports zero field radius/height mismatches, zero double edges, a pointer cursor on every clickable, and the report is attached to the delivery.
origin: founder

text: [founder] In a client app, data and highlight colour is the brand accent, not a new semantic colour: Sellify charts, "running/active" markers, survivor or winner call-outs and selected/followed states use the brand orange (`--ds-brand-signal`, soft fills `--ds-brand-signal-soft`), exactly like the app's existing charts (the brand page's launch-trends line). Green stays only for success feedback (saved, copied, approved status badge). Chart marks share the app's softness: bars get rounded caps (about 6px on a ~30px bar), legend swatches are dots, gridlines dashed and quiet. Before shipping a new chart or status, find its nearest sibling in the app and match colour, radius and stroke.
why: Founder on the Ad Spy brand page Tests chart (green stacked bars with 3px square tops, green dots and green Survivor badges): "usually our color would be orange yk not green and stuff a bit more rounded cuz that's everywhere else seen with consistency and you fuck it up and all EVERYWHERE check for this cmon each single small detail".
applies: charts, status markers and selected states inside an existing app.
check: new chart/status colours resolve to the app's accent tokens (grep the diff for new uses of success/green outside success messages); bar corner radius >= 4px; a side-by-side with the nearest existing chart in the same app.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Sweep the whole diff, not the screen you were asked about: after any feedback, grep every changed file for the same class of drift (off-accent colours, hex values, one-off radii, off-scale sizes and weights, stray shadows) and fix all of them, including ones inherited from older code on the same screen, in the same round. The founder reads one crop as a symptom of a habit.
why: Same message: "and all EVERYWHERE check for this cmon each single small detail".
check: the reply lists the sweep (patterns, hit count, what was fixed, what was deliberately kept and why).
origin: founder

text: [founder] No dead white space between related things. When one item in a row grows (a redo note opens, an error appears, a video card has an extra row), its siblings must not open empty gaps inside their content: transient inputs open as an overlay or popover on the item itself, equal-height cards keep their content stacked top-down with normal gaps and put the flexible space only above the action row, and two-column modals keep both columns filled or make the short one sticky.
why: Founder on the avatar review (one open redo note stretched every view in the row), Ad Spy cards (the link floating far under the text) and the ad detail modal (an empty left column): "at some places there is so much white space to other components that it looks just stupid... cmon and proper spacing".
check: open every transient state (note, error, menu) and screenshot the whole row: no sibling's gap between two of its own blocks grows; inside a card, gap between consecutive content blocks <= 16px except above the action row.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Every popup is rebuilt from the app's own dialog grammar, never shipped as an ad-hoc layout: header (title + one-line description), plain stacked fields (label 14/500, 8px to the control, 16px between groups), lists as option rows like the app's Select menu (hover tint, check on the selected row, own max-height scroll, ellipsis for long names), no boxed grey container inside the dialog, no uppercase section labels, no tinted selected rows, no focus ring visible on open, footer with Cancel (ghost) left of the primary. Test it with long names, many items and empty.
why: Founder on the Ad Spy "Save to boards" dialog (boxed grey board list, uppercase BOARDS, checkboxes with an orange-tinted row, orange focus ring on open, cramped tags, overflow with long names): "found a popup which I don't even want to talk about how bad it is and needs full redesign using our components, design language and all".
check: each popup screenshot shows one edge, one rhythm, owner components only; long-name and many-items states render without overflow.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Overlays (dialogs, popovers, menus, selects, sheets, toasts) have exactly one edge and a clean shadow: the edge lives in one place (a 1px ring at ~8% ink inside the overlay shadow token, border transparent), the shadow is tight (about 0 2px 4px -1px at 6% plus 0 12px 28px -8px at 14%), never a visible border plus a ring and never a wide 50px haze. Fix it in the shared owner components and the token, not per screen. Nothing inside an overlay is cut off: max-height calc(100dvh - 32px) with one inner scroll area. Nesting alternates surfaces: a box inside a white overlay is grey (work surface) and fields inside that grey box are white; fields directly on the white overlay keep the app field fill.
why: Founder on the Ad Spy detail modal and follow popover: "still with popups stuff cut off... the boxes are white bg, they should be gray and input fields on gray to be white... all popups or popovers feature ugly double border and just not good styled shadow... you didn't go through everything and fix stuff".
check: for each overlay: computed border is 0 or transparent while box-shadow carries the ring; bottom edge of content visible at 900px tall; nested box fill differs from its parent and from its fields.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Product showcase frames for video: the product sits on a near-black stage (#0C0C0D) with the same gap on the left, top and bottom (about 56px at 1220x900, 150px at 4K), the product's full height visible and only the right edge cropped (about 90% shown); generous corner radius (~22px), a 1px alpha ring and a soft low shadow (no heavy drop). State gaps in output pixels when talking 4K: 192px at 4K is 72 CSS px, not 192.
why: Founder on the Kite showcase (2026-10-15): "why is 192px so huge", "why the bottom is not shown", "wtf is left gap not the same as from top and bottom", "shadows a bit too strong", then "yess, this is correct... gaps a bit smaller... show a bit more of the right side", bg "use 0C0C0D".
applies: product showcase stills and load-in videos.
check: measured left = top = bottom gap; frame bottom inside the canvas; visible share of the product 85-95%.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Showcase load-ins move as one slow wave, not a sequence: every component rises together (start offsets ~80ms, each settling over ~1.6s on expo-out, ~28px travel), the signature visual resolves inside its card while it rises (Kite: the dot map dithers in pixel by pixel, a left-to-right sweep with per-dot jitter and 3-step opacity), and the payoff state (alert, flare, tooltip) lands as the wave settles (~1.6-2s), never after a wait. No light bars or scan flashes across the product; no single component appearing alone first.
why: Founder on Kite showcase rounds: map-first order "not smooth nor normal... everything similarly same time", the scan beam was a "flash slide", the fast wave "happens too fast and not premium", "you must wait too long for notifications to appear"; the slow wave + pixel map was "amazing".
applies: product load-in animations for showcase videos and heroes.
check: contact sheet at 0.3/0.8/1.2/1.6/2.0/3.0s: every card present by 0.8s, map fully resolved by ~1.6s, alert visible by ~2s.
origin: founder

text: [founder] A promo or offer visual on an existing brand is built from that brand's own product kit, not imitated: the offer becomes the brand's own product (Kaching's BFCM tiers = the catalogue's Bundles quantity-break card selling Kaching apps), with the kit's exact rows, tags, selection frame, hover/press veils and tokens. Keep it centred and Title Case like the brand's other heroes, low contrast (white options, an 8% tint selection, never a solid filled card), the brand's neutral grey as the base and the accent only on what is picked; the accent can deepen tier by tier (grey to full blue) and every accent surface (frame, figure, progress line, card field, title gradient) follows one shared state and fills in one direction (left to right). Show fine print as the card's own small text, not a paragraph under the hero; highlight the copy's dates and discount a step heavier and darker (600, #444), never black.
why: Founder on the Kaching BFCM hero (2026-10-19), across ~14 rounds: split layouts, dither charts, stat cards, a staircase and custom pills were "ass", "not our brand", "too crowded"; the Bundles-card version was "a good idea"; a solid button-face selection was "not that contrasty, just simple and nice movement"; dither inside the option boxes "ugly"; replaying icon animations on click "rejump"; then "it's amazing" once the grey base, blue-deepening tiers, grey-to-blue frame wash and a selection-linked title gradient (filling from the left) were in.
applies: offer, pricing-tier and promo visuals on existing brands.
check: every style value traces to the brand's kit tokens; no element re-animates on a repeat click; the accent appears only on the picked option; one state drives all accent fills in one direction.
origin: founder

text: [founder] "Clean" never means sparse. A hero or post component must carry Kestrel/Quorum density: a real app with its chrome (sidebar or rail, header, controls, 10+ meaningful data points), a material field behind it (halftone, grain gradient, dotted canvas or a lit scene), and one AI or decision moment. A data-viz made of a few big empty bars on a flat canvas is hollow, however tidy. A post card fills 50-70% of a square frame (Kargul posts), sits on a rich field, and shows a moment mid-interaction (a cursor, a drag, a running step), not a static form.
why: Founder on Overlap (light editorial hero over a 6-row timezone timeline, and a small find-a-time card on flat grey): "interesting style but not even close to being correct nor professional... just feels too hollow and stupid cmonnn retry from scratch".
check: count distinct UI data points in the product (>= 10) and filled area: product + field cover >= 60% of the fold; post card width >= 50% of the frame; background is a material, not one flat fill.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Never ship from memory or vibe: before any delivery run `tools/design_view.mjs` and read its PNG (the candidate beside the accepted and benchmark references at the same size, plus measured checks). A reference is a floor to build on, not a costume to copy: replicating one benchmark's surface (Taxo's serif campaign headline over silk, Marcel's palette on our content) while dropping the engine's own accepted rules (product in the hero, 52-72px Title Case headline, 2-line subtitle, solid post canvas, square or 16:9 post crop) is the failure. Every new attempt starts from founder-taste + the accepted builds, then adds the study.
why: Founder after Weft v3 (Taxo-replica hero with no product, 120px one-line serif; Marcel-palette post): "you forgot all the fucking rules, all the tries, all the studies... you just threw out... could you build out a design view for yourself what is a good X post or design in general... from the size to the style".
check: `reports/<name>/design-view.json` fails == 0, attached to the delivery.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Component posts run lighter than affectUI's measured greys and are built to be shared: tray #f6f6f6 (not #f0f0f0), rings at 6-6.5% ink, tiles #f8f8f8, canvas #fbfbfb, and one short line of copy where a paragraph would go. A still card is not a post; ship the component as an 8-12s loop where it does its one job (cursor travels, presses, the control works, morphs into its result, the strip's status chip rolls to the new state, then resets), with the first frame as the money frame.
why: Founder on the expense card v2 (Flo tray grammar, #f0f0f0): "ehhh grays a bit dark and just not clean and interesting viral.. not". X data agrees: single images 0.76x median engagement, component loops the most-posted format.
check: tray luminance >= #f5f5f5; a loop video exists next to the still; caption-free media.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Work replicate-first (docs/REPLICATE-FIRST.md): every new piece starts from one named reference the founder rates (AlignUI, affectUI/Flo, Kargul, Rico, Attio), rebuilt at its pixel size, overlaid with `tools/compare.mjs` until rows, columns, dividers and edges register within ~4px, then given our content and 1-3 owned touches. Build only what was asked: no animation, extra states or sections unless named.
why: Founder after the Share and Expense rejects: "I did not ask to animate... the spacing the roundness the components the colors everything is just not good... form not being centered... just try replicating a few works of theirs (in terms of style with your own touch that would be backed up by the book and your checks)... create a way to work like we used to".
check: `work/<name>/cmp-*-overlay.png` exists and registers; DIRECTION.md names the reference and lists the owned touches.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Bento cells and component posts need styling, not just UI in a white box: build each bento cell as a lit object scene (Clerk/Raycast grammar in light mode): a soft spotlight from above over a faint dot grid on a #fbfbfb to #f4f4f5 cell, one tactile object made from the product (white objects with ring + inner top highlight + contact + soft drop; the hero element raised in the accent with a gradient fill, inner shade and a tinted drop), staggered-opacity lists, a little depth (one tilt, one lifted card), and the copy small at the bottom (15/500 title + 14 muted). Component posts get the same lit canvas and at least one crafted object (date tile, raised accent button).
why: Founder on the first Cadence bento and event card (flat white cards with UI inside): "the component and bento straight up ass, nothing cool about them, no cool stylings or stuff".
check: every cell has one tactile object with the 4-part shadow and a spotlight; no cell is only a white card with rows.
origin: founder

text: [founder] The bento style the founder loves: Kargul's services-bento grammar, one monochrome isometric line drawing per cell of the product's own object (iso plates, stacked layers, extruded towers) with shared hatching, dot fills, diamond nodes, dashed guide lines and a faint perspective grid; title top-left, short body, caps chip row; one accent only on the answer. It must be drawn with precision and detail (uniform strokes, true projection, crisp joins), never as loose shapes. Learn from `knowledge/web/isometric-line-art.md` and build with `system/iso/`.
why: Founder on Cadence bento v3: "nowww we talking, yess this style is amazing, yet ... it needs incredible precision and you could do wayyy better and more in detail ... marcel is goated at this too". Earlier v1/v2 (white cards, mixed lit objects) were "noobish".
check: every cell uses the same iso system and stroke ladder; one accent per cell.
origin: founder

text: [founder] For feature/bento line art, Linear is the bar ("check linear, they do it good enough"): a two-tone statement headline, columns split by 1px hairlines with mono FIG labels, ONE quiet object per column in 2:1 dimetric, every edge the same 1px hairline (~36% ink on white), white faces, no hatch, grain, nodes, guides, callouts or colour; the idea is told by geometry alone (the raised or lifted piece is the answer); small title + muted line at the bottom. Kit: `system/iso` with `mode="hairline" kind="dimetric"`.
why: Founder after the Kargul-grammar v4 with callouts, hatch and violet: "check linear cmon they do it good enough, not u".
applies: feature sections and bentos with iso art.
check: one stroke weight in the art; zero fills other than white; no accent colour.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Do not abstract the bento into meaningless geometry: Linear-style slabs, combs and bars with shading ("interesting yet stupid and not nice at all") lose to the Kargul-grammar cells that draw the product's own objects (calendar layers, the focus block, the moved meeting, the booking card, the day towers) with callouts that name the answer. Take precision and restraint from Linear, but keep the subject from the product; shading stays subtle (tint families, low glow), never a saturated solid block.
why: Founder on the shaded Linear-style figures, 2026-10-21.
check: every figure is recognisably the product's own object and names its answer.
origin: founder

text: [founder] Iso bento art is not done until one reference cell is replicated pixel for pixel: before drawing our own scenes, rebuild one Kargul services-bento cell (knowledge/benchmarks/bento/kargul-services-bento.png) at its exact scale and overlay it with `tools/compare.mjs` until the plates, nodes, hatch, dot fills, icon glyphs and labels register within ~2px. Our marks (invented icons, circles, random colours, dot nodes) read generic; only measured copies of his construction carry the craft.
why: Founder on bento v4-shaded: "stuff is just very very much off... from icons you drew to circles to colors to points and how everything looks, it's generic and not good at all".
check: `work/replicas/cmp-kargul-iso-overlay.png` registers before new scenes ship.
origin: founder

text: [founder-process] Start every Sellify UI task by fetching `origin/main`, merging it into the local design branch, and listing teammates' commits in the area; adopt their logic and naming before touching visuals.
why: "have you got the latest versions and updated what we designed to them... if christian did anything" (2026-10-20). Our Ad Spy Tests tab duplicated Aaron's ENG-2232 because the branch was a day stale.
check: branch is 0 behind origin/main at handoff; report lists teammate commits adopted.

text: [founder-process] Run the component checklist on every screen before handoff: shared owner and system API (no lookalikes); radius 12/16/20; type 12/14/18 at 450/500 with no tracking or leading classes; orange (brand-signal) only for data, selected and active, green only for success; one edge per box and overlay with the single overlay shadow; grey sections holding white items, with white fields inside white popups; ghost Cancel; no dead white space; long names and many items; cursor and hover on everything clickable; no clipping or horizontal scroll at 390.
why: "triple check every component, then the affectui alignui style" (2026-10-20), and the repeated catches: green chart, square bars, double popup borders, white boxes in white popups, dead space under a redo note.
check: a written pass/fail per screen in the session report.
origin: founder

text: [founder-process] When a fix is asked as "the button", check the whole component around it against the checklist before calling it done.
why: ENG-2510: the first round only fixed the hidden Analyze button. "did you actually fix stuff to make it properly like in our design style" led to "Your upload", empty rows dropped and the orange saved icon.
check: the report lists the surrounding issues found, not only the asked one.
origin: founder

text: [founder-process] For a reported bug or ticket, reproduce it on the real local route with data like the reporter's (upload through the product's own flow), then deliver a side-by-side of the reporter's screenshot and the fixed live page.
why: "show me the result in action so I could see where what they were talking about" (2026-10-19).
check: a before/after PNG exists in the ticket folder.
origin: founder

text: [founder-process] Explain status in plain words: what was asked, what was done, where it lives (branch, folder), and what Augustas has to do. No jargon dumps.
why: "what are they simply so I could understand" (2026-10-20).
check: each item fits in about three lines.

text: [founder-process] PRs only on an explicit "create a PR": base on latest main, authored as Augustas, no AI or tool tags, description from `.github/generate-pr-description.md`, screenshots on the `pr-assets` branch under `pr-<number>/`.
why: "never look like it's made by not human" (2026-10-19), and the AGENTS.md screenshot rule.
check: `git log --format=%an` and the PR body contain no AI mention.

text: [founder-process] Never set up session-sharing tools (Traces) or anything that publishes agent sessions.
why: "don't do that... let's have everything personally" (2026-10-20).
check: no `traces` hooks in agent config.

text: [founder] No borderless filled boxes anywhere: every grey or filled box, list, value field or summary bar gets the quiet 1px border.
why: "we don't really have borderless components... it should feature a border as everything else" (Story structure list, Current photo, Charged-so-far bar, Scene details fields all shipped borderless).
check: no element has a non-transparent background with a 0px border inside a surface.

text: [founder] Nested radii are concentric: inner radius = outer radius − padding between them; a nested box never looks rounder or sharper than its parent allows.
why: "popups where the roundness of the rectangle is not properly configured relative to the outside box... and roundness below the video, why so much".
check: computed inner radius ≈ outer radius − gap.

text: [founder] A choice between options that carry descriptions uses selectable option cards (icon, title, description, radio/check; selected = soft orange fill, orange border, filled orange check), not a sliding segmented control. Segmented controls are for short labels only.
why: "instead of sliding, a full box or some component where you select one or another would be better UI and UX".
check: no segmented control has a description line under its options.

text: [founder] All pills and chips are one component: same height, padding and font, text vertically centred, and pills in one row share a centre line with the title beside them.
why: "the length 10s and Not made, both pills and they aren't vertically spaced... you miss this A LOT".
check: measure the pill boxes in a row: identical height and centre y.

text: [founder] Sibling collections look like one family: a populated grid uses the same tile system (columns, media ratio, chips on media, meta type) as its empty-state or template tiles.
why: "why is the after for the library ass and different from the correct version which is beautiful" (library cards vs template tiles).

text: [founder] Sticky pay and action bars show key facts as small bordered pills with one quiet note line, spaced well clear of the primary button, never as two cramped text lines.

text: [founder] Any list or timeline must be designed and tested for its real range (for example 2, 5 and 12+ scenes), with no truncation that hides meaning.
why: "it gets cramped for bigger videos, so think of a solution... fully configured and tested".

text: [founder] Status visuals are styled with intent: done = quiet check, current = orange plus motion, pending = grey ring; no heavy black filled checks. Add tasteful motion (progress, current step, enter, selection), respecting reduced motion.
why: "regarding the orange colours and use of black checkboxes, just style the colours and icons there better... and animations everywhere also cool".

text: [founder] Every confirm or cost dialog uses the full studio dialog (header, bordered summary box with the facts, footer with ghost Cancel); a bare title-line-two-buttons dialog counts as unstyled.
why: "I've found a completely unstyled popup, how did you miss that".

text: [founder] Borders are 1px everywhere, with no 2px borders, outlines or rings on fields, dropdowns, cards, tiles or selected states. Focus = 1px edge in the focus colour plus the soft 10% halo (box-shadow); selected = 1px orange edge plus a soft halo.
why: "the fucking 2 px borders... nowhere even on dropdowns, we don't have 2px borders, only 1px" (avatars redo note overlay, 2026-10-20).
check: no computed border/outline width of 2px or more (except intentional dividers) on any interactive or surface element, at rest and focused.

text: [founder] A pill or chip inside a selected (orange-filled) card is white with a quiet border, never orange-on-orange; on an unselected card it may be orange.
why: "a fully orange pill in an orange stuff... the pill should be white if it's selected and in orange background".

text: [founder] The page's top offset to the first section equals the side gutter; spacing to the frame is equal on all sides.

text: [founder] (REVISED 2026-10-22) Media review grids use ONE standard tile ratio per grid (the kit 9:16 for video frames, 3:4 for set or sheet images), object-fit cover, full image only in the enlarge lightbox; empty, failed and making tiles are the same size. Grids are designed for volume (1, 3, 12, 20+), with aligned actions, a counter and bulk approve; long status or error messages live in one bordered status box and never shift the actions.

text: [founder] Nothing overlaps or overflows its container: step trays, pills and labels truncate or scroll instead; test the longest real list (for example 8 steps).

text: [T5] Use icon + label in menus for complex or abstract functions: each item (New Tab, New Incognito, Recent Tabs, Downloads, History, Bookmark) gets a leading outline icon plus its text; bad = label only.

text: [T37] Put the most important pages at the corners of the tab bar (serial position effect): good order Home, Search, Chat, Cart, Profile (Home first, Profile last); bad order Search, Home, Cart, Profile, Chat.

text: [T9] Show a progress bar for multi-step flows: 3 steps with step 1 a green check, current step 2 a green numbered node, step 3 grey, solid green connector for done and dashed for remaining, step names below.

text: [T44] Limit card content: truncate description with an ellipsis and add an "Explore More"/"See more" button; never make a card's text scroll internally (bad shows an inner scrollbar).

text: [T45] Use swipe actions on list rows (swipe reveals a red trash and a green star circle button) instead of a "..." menu button on every row.

text: [T53] For homogeneous content use a list (one container, hairline separators) instead of a stack of separate cards.

text: [T85] Limit links in a card: one link or a limited set of actions. Good: plain body text, a filled "Primary Action" and an underlined "Secondary Action"; bad: also two inline blue underlined links in the paragraph.

text: [T76] Avoid the super-minimal look in list rows: add detail ("Episode #1" instead of "#1", a progress bar with "42%" and a cancel x, rather than a bare bar).

text: [T7] Use one consistent icon set: the page's good example shows three coherent sets in rows (A filled circle, B outline ring, C plain line) while the bad mixes filled circle plus, outline trash and outline cart.

text: In a two-button confirmation dialog, set both buttons the same size side by side, the dismissive/neutral option on the left in a light grey fill and the emphasised option on the right; the emphasised slot holds the safe recommended answer in primary colour ("Don't Cancel", T8) or the destructive answer in red ("Yes, Delete", T12). Inside an inline form the order flips: the filled primary ("Login") sits first, left-aligned under the fields, with grey "Cancel" to its right (as drawn on p.14, p.67, p.103).

text: [team research] Keep a tracked uppercase/mono eyebrow only when it identifies a real taxonomy, status, date, edition, location or sequence, that information would be useful without the styling, and the same label system is used consistently. Otherwise remove it and let the heading establish hierarchy, write a natural-language context line, integrate the category into the headline, or use placement/scale instead.

text: [team research] Do not enlarge a sentence headline until it fills most of the viewport with extreme tracking and forced breaks. Keep it only when language is the brand artifact, the words deserve the stage, letterforms and breaks were composed, and the hero stays balanced at intermediate and narrow widths. Better: medium display scale with image/grid/whitespace leading; one word or typographic detail carrying emphasis; a compact editorial title tied to evidence; reveal scale later.

text: [team research] Do not default to a floating pill dock (centred glass capsule with logo, segmented nav, white or accent CTA). Keep it only when floating solves a real spatial/persistent-tool need, the site has few destinations and the geometry belongs to the identity, the background makes translucency meaningful, and mobile stays clear. Better: edge-aligned header on the page grid; brand-specific masthead; quiet transparent header with no outer shell; conventional header distinguished by type, spacing or content.

text: [team research] Do not build a "designed-to-look-designed" CTA (wide rounded rectangle with inner arrow chip, liquid fill, magnetic hover, rotating arrow). Keep inner structure only if it communicates a real state or split action, motion explains direction/progress, and the target stays stable. Better: a plain well-proportioned solid control with specific copy; a typographic link for low commitment; a brand-derived shape used consistently; a familiar button with a distinctive pressed/focus/material response.
why: Too many parts for a simple action; it performs "premium" instead of building confidence.
check: count of decorative behaviours on CTA <= 1; target does not move on hover.

text: [team research] Lowercase as borrowed personality: when wordmark, nav, buttons, headings and body are all lowercase there is no contrast between brand voice and functional language. Keep it only when the wordmark is intentionally drawn that way, the tone supports intimacy, and functional labels still follow coherent casing; otherwise preserve sentence/title case in nav and actions, reserve lowercase for the wordmark or one expressive role, use wording not casing for warmth. (Note: this is the exact voice Larpo's own site uses; see `larpo-brand-and-constraints.md` LBC-06 and conflict C2.)

text: [team research] Use five layers: strategic (visitor, painful moment, desired change, first objection, proof, action commitment); brand (three traits + one contradiction, translated into observable behaviour: "calm" may mean stable layouts, low motion amplitude, generous blank space, plain action language, not automatically beige); product (one workflow mapped as states: source/input, processing, draft, human review, outcome, recovery/error/history); identity (wordmark and symbol behaviour, typefaces, colour roles, spacing density, corner and line logic, image/illustration grammar, motion grammar, one signature motif); marketing composition (chosen only after the others).

text: [team research] Use the strongest evidence available: (1) real interactive product behaviour, (2) real product screenshot with truthful data, (3) deterministic prototype with a labelled sample workflow, (4) annotated before/after with explicit assumptions, (5) diagram of the actual mechanism, (6) abstract visual metaphor. Abstract visuals are weakest as proof but can be strongest as identity; keep those jobs separate.

text: [team research] A fictional company needs recorded internal truth: product name and pronunciation; category and narrow wedge; primary user and current workaround; input, transformation, output and human-control points; pricing logic or sales motion; plausible sample dataset; one limitation or tradeoff; one reason it can exist now. text: [team research] Failure modes to avoid: a product name chosen only because it sounds like a startup; a logo drawn before a semantic territory; a font chosen from a screenshot not tested with the real name; fake charts that do not support the promise; three font families + five radii + several effect languages competing for "premium"; an elaborate shader that makes the CTA unreadable; a screenshot impressive only at full size that collapses to gray noise in a feed.

text: [team research] A typeface must pass two tests: semantic fit (structure supports the brand voice) and operational fit (weights, glyphs, metrics, numerals, features, files, licence). text: On text-heavy pages put the key point in the first two paragraphs, begin headings with the most informative words, and break runs of text with lists and bolded terms.
why: Users scan in F-shaped/layer-cake patterns and miss the right and lower lines.
check: first heading text begins with a noun phrase from the topic; no paragraph over ~5 lines without a structural break.

text: Body text: 15-25 px on the web; line spacing 120-145% of font size; line length 45-90 characters (Every Layout caps the measure at 60ch as its single axiom).
why: Longer lines need more leading; the eye loses its place past ~90 characters.
check: computed font-size, line-height/font-size, and `ch` width of `p` (characters per line from rendered text).

text: Pick the canvas from one of two measured families. Family 1, tinted near-black: page L 0.134-0.195 (Linear `#08090a` L 0.139, Raycast `#07080a` 0.134, GitHub `#0d1117` 0.176, PlanetScale `#111111` 0.178, Cursor `#14120b` 0.182, Railway `#13111c` 0.186, Supabase `#131413` 0.190). Family 2, true `#000` canvas (Vercel, Resend, Framer, Neon) where every raised surface is an opaque step at L 0.145-0.22. Do not invent a canvas at L < 0.13 that is not true black.
why: below L ~0.13 a tinted canvas stops separating from OLED black and the card step has no room; true black works only because the next step is large (+0.145 to +0.21) and carries the structure.
check: compute page background OKLCH L: in [0.134, 0.195] or exactly #000 with first surface L in [0.145, 0.22]. Nocturne `#05060a` = L 0.123 (outside both).

text: Use smooth corners where the corner is large enough to be seen: app/record tiles and avatars (any size, they read as objects), cards and frames at R >= 20px, hero product windows. Below R ~12px, or below 0.4 smoothing, a squircle is indistinguishable from `border-radius` and costs a clip path for nothing.
why: Fit at R 96: smoothing 0.2 differs from a plain radius by 10 px² over the whole corner and 0.4 by 27 px², both about 0.1px of mean offset. The best native match for both is plain `round` at the same radius. At R 12 the run-in difference (1.17R vs 0.95R) is about 2.6px, which survives only on large-radius objects.
check: squircle used only where R >= 20 or the element is an icon/avatar tile; smoothing >= 0.5 wherever used.

text: Never write `corner-shape: squircle` to mean "iOS corner". The native equivalent of Figma 60% / Apple is `border-radius: calc(R * 1.2); corner-shape: superellipse(1.32)` (use `nativeCornerFor(R, s)` from `squircle.ts` for other smoothings: 0.8 → `superellipse(1.76)` at 1.56R, 1.0 → `superellipse(2.2)` at 2.14R).
why: `squircle` (K 2, exponent 4) at radius R puts the apex at 0.23R; it matches a plain radius of 0.6R and reads boxy. Superellipse corners are drawn inside the radius box, so any K > 1 needs a larger radius to look equally soft. Resend raises the radius under `@supports (corner-shape: squircle)` (rounded-2xl/3xl), and Framer scales its fallback to 0.752x.

text: Give a smoothed corner its room: each corner consumes `(1 + smoothing) * R` of every edge it touches, so a uniform squircle needs the short side >= `2 * (1 + s) * R` (3.2R at 0.6). Below that, Figma (and `squircle.ts`, `preserveSmoothing: false`) reduces the smoothing automatically. Pills (R = h/2) stay plain `border-radius: 999px`; never squircle a pill or a 32px button at R 12+.
why: figma-squircle budget = min(w,h)/2 per corner, distributed largest corner first. Apple's own clamp is `MIN(w,h)/2/1.52866`. A 40px button at R 14 has p = 22.4 > 20, so the smoothing collapses and the shape is a plain corner anyway.
check: for squircle elements: min(w,h) >= 3.2R; pills use circular radius.

text: In the SVG fallback: - **Clip:** `clip-path: path()`, regenerated by a ResizeObserver. - **Border and ring:** clip-path clips them, so draw them as an even-odd SVG band between two offsets of the shape (exact width at every point). - **Blurred shadows:** put them on an unclipped sibling with `border-radius = R`, because blur >= 4px hides the corner difference. - **drop-shadow:** use `filter: drop-shadow()` only for contact shadows tighter than 4px, since it has no spread and costs a filter pass per layer.

text: Nest squircles concentrically: the inner shape is the outer shape inset by the padding, with radius = outer R − inset and the same smoothing (`getSquirclePath({ ...outer, inset })`). Never put a circular inner radius in a squircle frame, or a squircle inside a circular one.
why: Vercel's interface guidelines: "Child radius <= parent radius & concentric so curves align". Mixed corner families show as a changing gap along the corner, because the run-ins differ by 0.2R.
applies: cards in frames, buttons in toolbars, icons in tiles.
check: nested pair: inner R = outer R − padding (±1px), same corner family.

text: Dither and grain are different tools. Dither (Larpo's pixel dither) is a visible pattern used as the signature field, governed by founder-taste. Grain is invisible tooth that removes banding and plastic smoothness. Never stack dither and grain on the same area, and never let grain alone be "the signature".
why: - The founder asks for a crafted signature field in every hero (live dither, halftone, shader, real-data map). - Grain at .03-.08 cannot carry that. - Doubling the noise turns the dither's deliberate pixels to mud. - Kaching and Capto (shipped) use dither bands with clean surfaces around them.

text: Never put glass on glass. Keep one glass material per stack, and at most 3 glass surfaces per viewport. Treat Apple's Liquid Glass (refraction via SVG `feDisplacementMap` in `backdrop-filter: url()`) as Chromium-only progressive enhancement for the navigation layer, never for content cards.
why: - WWDC25 session 219: Liquid Glass is "best reserved for the navigation layer; avoid glass on glass". - Two variants (Regular and Clear) that should never be mixed. - `backdrop-filter: url()` works only in Chrome (kube.io). - Displacement maps rebuild on resize.

text: Never scale or skew a stroked element. Project points in code and emit screen-space paths; render the SVG 1:1 (width = viewBox width); add `vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke"` only as a guard.
why: An SVG `matrix()` on a stroked group shears the stroke (thick on one axis, thin on the other) and stretches dashes; non-scaling-stroke fixes width but dash behaviour under transforms is not guaranteed (open question 1).
check: grep the art: no `transform=` on any element with a stroke; no `patternTransform` with scale.

text: Build every curve in the object's own plane as cubic Beziers (rounded corners, circles via k = 0.5523) and project the control points; never draw an ellipse by eye.
why: A parallel projection is affine and affine maps preserve Beziers, so the result is the exact projected circle (on the top plane a 1.732:1 ellipse at 0deg); eyeballed ellipses are the first amateur tell.
check: an iso circle's bbox ratio = 1.732 (top plane); corner arcs tangent to both edges.
source: [engine note]; IBM (curves from quarter circles on the grid).

text: Responsiveness (INP): animation must not delay the next paint after input. INP measures worst interaction latency (input delay + handler + next frame) at p75: **good <=200ms, needs improvement 200-500ms, poor >500ms**. Long tasks delay event handling; don't start heavy JS animation setup inside click handlers; yield (e.g., `scheduler.yield()`), and don't gate UI updates on animation completion.
check: field INP / CrUX; lab: DevTools "Interactions" track.

text: Start every spring at no overshoot (Motion `bounce: 0`, i.e. damping ratio 1). Add `bounce` 0.1-0.25 only for drag-release, swipe-dismiss or deliberately playful elements; never above 0.3 on product UI.

Feedback must reveal the (invisible) rules; give feedback within ~100ms of the trigger [engine note: the 0.1s figure is the classic Nielsen response limit, not fetched here]. Long-lived loops should decay: the 50th occurrence must be quieter than the 1st.
why: Rules are invisible; feedback is how users learn them (Saffer).

text: Order matters: a standalone `@starting-style` block has the same specificity as the rule it modifies and must come **after** it; nested form is `selector { @starting-style { ... } }`. It applies only to CSS transitions (CSS animations don't need it). It supplies "from" values on first render and on `display:none` -> visible. It is **not** used on the way out; exit goes to the element's default state, so entry/exit can differ.

why: Real springs (Motion) keep velocity on interruption; this does not. Use for static hover/entry states, not drag release.

text: Same-document: feature-detect, then wrap the DOM update. If page visibility is `hidden` the transition is skipped. Duplicate `view-transition-name` values at once reject `ready` and skip the transition. ```js function go(update) { if (!document.startViewTransition) return update(); document.startViewTransition(() => update()); } ``` (React: wrapping `flushSync` for the DOM update is the usual companion; or use React's `<ViewTransition>` inside `startTransition`, see `motion-library-react.md`/React docs where `enter/exit/update/share/default` props map to CSS classes and React does NOT auto-handle reduced motion.)

text: Default animation is cross-fade + smooth geometry; customise with `::view-transition-group(name)`, `-image-pair`, `-old`, `-new`. Targeting `*` styles all snapshots. Keep durations to the motion tokens: 250-350ms for route changes. ```css @keyframes fade-in  { from { opacity: 0; } } @keyframes fade-out { to   { opacity: 0; } } ::view-transition-group(root) { animation-duration: 280ms; animation-timing-function: cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1); } ::view-transition-old(root) { animation: 140ms ease-in both fade-out; } ::view-transition-new(root) { animation: 280ms var(--ease-out) both fade-in; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { ::view-transition-group(*), ::view-transition-old(*), ::view-transition-new(*) { animation: none !important; } } ``` The reduced-motion block is my application of React's documented approach (their docs set `animation: none` under the media query) [engine note: for a minimal-change variant keep a crossfade only].

text: Prefer CSS/WAAPI for predetermined animations (off-thread), JS for dynamic/interruptible ones. WAAPI snippet with `fill: "forwards"` and a custom easing string is hardware accelerated for compositor properties: ```js el.animate([{ clipPath: "inset(0 0 100% 0)" }, { clipPath: "inset(0 0 0 0)" }], { duration: 600, fill: "forwards", easing: "cubic-bezier(0.77, 0, 0.175, 1)" }); ``` - CSS property cost cheat sheet [engine note, from the well-known CSS Triggers model; not fetched]: composite-only = `transform`, `opacity` (and `translate/scale/rotate`); paint-only = `color`, `background-color`, `box-shadow`, `border-radius`, `outline`, `visibility`; layout+paint = `width/height/top/left/margin/padding/font-size/border-width/flex-basis`. Josh Comeau also ranks `background-color` as moderately expensive and `height` as to-avoid (verified).

text: Where a border exists only for depth, use a layered, transparent `box-shadow` ring instead. text: Toasts (Sonner pattern): enter from `translateY(100%)` via a mounted flag or `@starting-style` with a CSS transition (about 400ms `ease`), leave in the same direction, stacked toasts offset about 14px with scale 1 - 0.05 x index, 4s default lifetime paused on hover and on `document.hidden`, bridge gaps with a pseudo-element, imperative API with one mount point.
why: Same-direction enter/exit makes swipe-to-dismiss intuitive; transitions survive rapid adds; hidden-tab pause prevents missed toasts.
check: `visual` + timers.
source: emil-design-eng "The Sonner Principles" (also in craft-emil-kowalski). [engine note] the 4s default conflicts with the accessibility rule in 2.12 for action/error toasts; follow 2.12.

text: Dismiss by velocity as well as distance: dismiss if `abs(distance) >= threshold` or `abs(distance)/elapsedMs > 0.11`; apply damping/friction past the boundary rather than a hard stop; call `setPointerCapture` once a drag starts; ignore additional touch points after the drag begins.

text: Swipe rows (Jakub's iOS-style example): `drag="x"` with `dragElastic` about 0.05 and `dragMomentum={false}` so the row lands on snap points (-116, 0, +116 px); commit threshold 58px; reveal action 1 at 44px and action 2 at 88px (pixel thresholds, not percentages); action buttons enter from opacity 0 / scale 0.5; indicators scale 0.75 with the origin at their corner; spring 0.3s bounce 0.
why: Fixed snap points make the outcome predictable; pixel thresholds are easy to tune.

text: For SF Pro (system-ui on Apple devices) do not impose a web-style negative curve: Apple's own table is +0.012em at 10pt, 0 at 12pt, -0.026em at 17pt (minimum), -0.023 at 20pt, +0.003 at 24pt, +0.014 at 28pt, +0.010 at 40pt, +0.004 at 64pt and 0 from 80pt; Apple.com sets SF Pro Display 600 at 80px/-0.015em and 56px/-0.005em, 17px text at -0.022em.

why: Each layer costs paint time, worst on cheap mobile GPUs (Comeau); drop-shadow follows the alpha shape that box-shadow cannot.
check: count layered-shadow elements in viewport <= 8.

text: Inputs: height = the button of the same tier (Geist 32/36/40, coss 32, Untitled UI and AlignUI 40), radius = the button radius, `1px` border or ring at ink .10 plus `0 1px 2px rgb(0 0 0/.05)` on a surface fill; on focus drop the small shadow, raise border to ink .34 or accent, and add a 3-4px outer ring at .16-.24 alpha (coss `ring-[3px]` accent at 24%, Geist `0 0 0 1px .34, 0 0 0 4px .16` light and .51/.24 white in dark, Untitled UI inset 2px #9e77ed).
why: One edge treatment from rest to focus keeps the field from jumping; the shadow removal on focus is what makes the ring read.
check: input height = adjacent button height; focus ring width 3-4px at alpha .16-.24 (or inset 2px accent).

text: Add the coss inner highlight to light surfaces: a `before` pseudo-element at `inset: 0` with `border-radius: calc(var(--radius) - 1px)` and `box-shadow: 0 1px rgb(0 0 0 / .04)` (dark: `0 -1px rgb(255 255 255 / .06)`), on top of `shadow-xs/5` and a 1px border.
why: It places a 1px light/dark edge inside the border so inputs, cards and menus read as slightly raised without a visible shadow; coss uses it on buttons (outline), inputs, cards, selects, menus and popovers.
check: surface has `::before` with 1px inset shadow of alpha .04-.06.

text: Default the hero h1 to weight 400-500; use 600+ only as a voice decision written in DIRECTION.md.
why: In 50 premium heroes, 20 set the h1 at 400-450 and 12 at 460-550; only 8 use 560-650 and 7 use 700+. The engine's default (Inter/Geist 600, tight) matches 16% of the sample and is why builds look alike.
check: computed h1 `font-weight`; if >= 560, DIRECTION.md names a voice whose spec is >= 560 (gothic-heavy, rounded-friendly, wide-extended, condensed-statement, variable-expressive, character-grotesk at 500+).

text: Every build picks exactly one voice from `system/variety/type-voices.json`, records its slug in DIRECTION.md, and does not reuse the voice of any of the last 4 ledger entries. Inter or Geist as the h1 face needs an `override:` line.
why: Only 9 of 50 premium h1s are Inter/Geist; 41 use other faces. Variety comes from the voice, not from tweaks to the same face.
check: DIRECTION.md contains `voice: <slug>`; h1 `font-family` first entry matches that voice's display family; slug not in the last 4 ledger fingerprints; h1 family not in {Inter, Geist} without an override.

text: Build a hand-set scale of 6-9 sizes seeded from a ratio, then adjust by eye. Landing/marketing: 1.2 at 360px interpolating to 1.333 at 1440px. Product UI: 1.125-1.2, fixed px steps. Never ship a ladder that is purely the framework default.
why: Ratios give coherence; hand adjustment gives fit (Refactoring UI advocates hand-picked scales over calculated ones [S]). Utopia's default pair is 1.2 -> 1.333 [P].
