text: Do not upscale rasters; target an intrinsic width of 1x-2x the rendered CSS width (cap DPR at 2) and use SVG for UI icons and line art.
why: Upscaled images look blurry; about 18% of GOV.UK sessions in Nov 2022 still reported DPR 1, so over-large sources waste their bandwidth.
check: `I5`: `naturalWidth >= clientWidth*min(DPR,2)*0.9` and `<= clientWidth*3`.
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/forms + https://web.dev/learn/images (+ web.dev lazy-loading, iframe lazy-loading, preload-responsive-images, replace-gifs-with-videos, image CDNs articles)

text: Use the native element whenever one exists (button, a, input+label, ul/ol, table, details, dialog, nav, main, headings). Add ARIA only for behaviour HTML cannot express (tabs, tree, live announcements, menus that really are application menus).
why: ARIA adds no behaviour; every role you assign makes you responsible for keyboard handling, focus and state. Correlation data: pages with ARIA show more detected errors.
check: static scan: `[role=button]:not(button,[type=button],[type=submit])`, `div[onclick],span[onclick]`, `a:not([href])[onclick]` must be zero unless allow-listed with a keyboard handler; axe `aria-allowed-role`, `aria-valid-attr-value` pass (extends `A1`/`A6` in implementation-craft).
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: Do not overwrite a native role. Do not put `role=button` on an `<a>`, `role=tab` on a heading, `role=heading` on a link. If a heading must live inside a tab, put the tab role on the wrapper and keep the heading inside it.
why: An ARIA role replaces the element's built-in semantics, so heading navigation, link lists or form behaviour are lost.
check: selector: `h1[role],h2[role],h3[role],h4[role],h5[role],h6[role]`, `a[role=button]`, `a[role=heading]` count 0; axe `aria-allowed-role`.
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: Every interactive control, native or ARIA, must be reachable and operable by keyboard. Use `tabindex="0"` to add something to tab order, `tabindex="-1"` for script-only focus, never a positive value. Do not add tab stops to headings or paragraphs.
why: Positive tabindex rewrites document order and strands keyboard and AT users; stops on inert text look like broken controls.
check: `[tabindex]:not([tabindex="0"]):not([tabindex="-1"])` count 0 (axe `tabindex`); for each `[tabindex="0"]` that is not natively interactive, assert a role plus a key handler exists or it is a scroll container.
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: Never hide something focusable from assistive technology: no `aria-hidden="true"` or `role=presentation|none` on a focusable element or on an ancestor that contains focusable descendants.
why: The element stays in tab order but is silent to screen readers, producing "ghost" focus.
applies: all (modals, off-canvas menus, carousels in particular).
check: `[aria-hidden="true"] :is(a[href],button,input,select,textarea,summary,[tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"]))` count 0; axe `aria-hidden-focus`.
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: Every interactive element has an accessible name before any other attribute is considered: link text, button text, `alt` on a linked image, an associated `<label>`. Verify in the accessibility tree.
why: Without a name a screen reader announces just "button" or "link" and the control is unusable.
check: axe `button-name`, `link-name`, `input-button-name`, `label`, `image-alt`, `select-name`, `aria-input-field-name`; Playwright `locator.ariaSnapshot()` shows a name for every `button`/`link`/`textbox`.
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: Avoid redundant or conflicting ARIA on elements that already carry the role (`ul role=list`, `summary role=button`, `nav role=navigation`, `form role=form`).
why: Redundant roles add noise; on `summary` the override can break native expand/collapse announcement.
check: `summary[role],nav[role=navigation],main[role=main],header[role=banner],footer[role=contentinfo],form[role=form]` count 0.
source: https://web.dev/learn/accessibility/aria-html. [engine note] Exception: `ul[role=list]` is sometimes added deliberately when `list-style:none` makes Safari/VoiceOver drop list semantics; allow-list that one case only.
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: Use HTML landmark elements; `section` and `form` become landmarks only when they have an accessible name, so name them or do not count on them. Have at least one landmark, one `main`.
why: Landmark lists are a primary screen-reader navigation method.
check: `main` count 1; `header,nav,main,footer,aside` present; `nav` siblings each have a distinct `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby`; axe `landmark-one-main`, `landmark-unique`, `region`.
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: Headings come from `h1-h6` elements in order, with no skipped levels; style the heading with classes independent of its level; never fake a heading with a styled div or `p`.
why: AT users navigate by heading level; faked headings do not exist in the tree.
check: axe `heading-order`, `empty-heading`; script: no element whose class matches `/\bh[1-6]\b|heading/` is a non-heading tag without `role=heading`; consecutive heading levels never jump by more than 1 descending (`A9`).
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: Group parallel items in real lists (`ul`, `ol`, `dl`) and never place `li` outside `ul/ol/menu`. A list-looking stack of divs or paragraphs is not a list.
why: Lists announce count and position; it also helps users with attention or reading difficulties scan.
check: axe `list`, `listitem`, `definition-list`; selector `div.ul,li:not(ul>li,ol>li,menu>li)` count 0.
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: Data tables: header cells are `th`, tables get a `caption` (or a heading immediately before), complex tables add `scope`, row groups, `colgroup`. Layout tables must have no `th`/`caption` and be hidden from AT with `role=presentation`; prefer CSS grid or flex over layout tables.
why: Header/cell relationships are what screen readers read while navigating cells.
check: for each `table:not([role=presentation],[role=none])`: `th` count >= 1 and (`caption` or accessible name) present; axe `th-has-data-cells`, `td-headers-attr`, `scope-attr-valid`.
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: Each page (and each SPA route) gets a unique, descriptive `<title>` that puts the page-specific part first and the site name last, kept to roughly 55-60 characters.
why: The title is the first thing announced; front-loading avoids repeating the site name every time; search engines truncate near 55-60 characters.
check: `document.title` length <= 60, does not start with the site name unless it is the home page, differs between routes; in SPAs assert `document.title` changes after client-side navigation.
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: Set `lang` on `<html>` to the page's primary language using a short code; mark foreign phrases with `lang` on a wrapper; never list multiple languages in the root `lang`.
why: Screen readers pick pronunciation rules from it; a missing value reads text with the user's default voice.
check: `html[lang]` matches `/^[a-z]{2,3}(-[A-Za-z]{2,4})?$/`; axe `html-has-lang`, `html-lang-valid`, `valid-lang`.
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: Every `iframe` that carries distinct content gets a `title` describing it (video embeds, maps, widgets).
why: Frames are announced by title; untitled frames are unlabeled regions.
check: `iframe:not([title])` count 0 (axe `frame-title`).
source: https://web.dev/learn/accessibility/more-html. [engine note] The module also tells you to set `scrolling="auto"`; that attribute is obsolete HTML, skip it and rely on CSS `overflow`.
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: Provide a skip link as the first focusable element, with text that says where it goes ("Skip to main content"), visible (or revealed) on focus, targeting the `main` id.
why: Repeated header navigation is expensive to tab through.
applies: any page with a header nav.
check: `A4`: first Tab stop is `a[href^="#"]`; after Enter, `document.activeElement` or the scroll target is inside `main`; skip link is visible when focused.
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: Focus order must match the visual and reading order. Be careful with CSS `order`, `flex-direction: *-reverse`, grid placement and absolute positioning that detach visual order from DOM order.
why: Jumping focus is disorienting for keyboard and screen magnifier users. The module also notes that RTL pages invert the expected direction.
check: Playwright: press Tab N times, record `getBoundingClientRect()` of each focused element, assert the sequence is monotonic in reading order for the page direction (rows top to bottom, within row inline-start to inline-end), allow documented exceptions; no positive `tabindex`.
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: Never remove the focus indicator (`outline: 0|none`) without a visible replacement. Custom indicators can be any shape (outline, border, underline, background shift) but must not depend on colour alone and need 3:1 contrast against what they sit on.
why: A sighted keyboard user otherwise cannot tell where they are.
check: `A3`; CSS scan: any rule `:focus{outline:none|0}` without `box-shadow`, `border`, `background` or `text-decoration` in the same rule is a failure; computed focus style differs from unfocused.
source: https://web.dev/learn/accessibility/focus. [engine note] The module calls the 3:1 target "Focus Appearance (Minimum)"; in WCAG 2.2 final that name does not exist, the 3:1 figure is from 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast, see section 5.
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: Use a small number of focus-indicator styles, chosen per element type (for example dotted underline for in-text links, rounded outline for buttons), and keep them consistent across the page.
why: Predictability; many competing focus looks cause confusion.
check: count distinct computed focus signatures (`outline-style/width/color`, `box-shadow`) across focusables, expect <= 4.
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: Attach click behaviour to native `button`/`a` elements. If a non-semantic element must trigger an action, it needs role, `tabindex=0`, and both Enter and Space handling (keydown/keyup).
why: Click handlers on divs work for mouse only; the keyboard activation comes free only with native controls.
check: find elements with listeners/`onclick` that are not `a[href],button,input,select,textarea,summary,[role]` (DevTools `getEventListeners` in a Playwright evaluate) and fail; `A1`.
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: In single-page apps, on route change update `document.title` and move focus deliberately: to the main container (with an `aria-live` announcement), to the skip link, or to the new top-level heading.
why: Without a reload nothing tells a screen reader that the page changed.
check: Playwright: click an internal link, assert `document.title` changed and `document.activeElement` is the new `h1[tabindex="-1"]`, `main[tabindex="-1"]` or skip link, or a live region received text.
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: A modal must contain focus (Tab and Shift+Tab cycle inside) until dismissed, and focus returns to the trigger on close. Test that keyboard users can neither leave nor get trapped without a dismiss path.
why: Background content must not be reachable while the modal is the only task; but no keyboard trap on non-modal UI.
source: https://web.dev/learn/accessibility/javascript and https://web.dev/learn/accessibility/test-manual (keyboard checklist). [engine note] The module says JavaScript is essential for the trap; with native `dialog.showModal()` the browser does it, see `adrian-roselli.md` AR-21.
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: Announce dynamic changes with a live region (`role=status`/`aria-live=polite` for FYI, `alert` for urgent). The region must be present in the DOM when the page loads and then have its text swapped; creating the region at the same moment as the message often fails. Framework "announcer" utilities exist for React, Angular and Vue.
why: Assistive tech watches regions it already knows about.
applies: toasts, form status, filters, cart updates.
check: `[role=status],[role=alert],[aria-live]` exist in server-rendered HTML for each place the app announces; Playwright sets text and reads the accessibility tree/mutation.
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: Be selective with state attributes. Use `aria-expanded` for disclosure and `aria-pressed` for toggle buttons where the information changes what a user must do; do not sprinkle state attributes everywhere.
why: Each exposed state is read aloud; unnecessary states are noise.
check: `[aria-expanded]` only on button/summary-like controls; `[aria-pressed]` only on buttons (`:not(button,[role=button])` count 0).
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: Classify each image before coding it: decorative (hide it: `alt=""`, CSS background, or `role=presentation|none`), informative (describe what it conveys), functional (describe the action, e.g. "Search", "Home"), complex (short alt plus a long description elsewhere via a link, `aria-describedby`, or `figure`/`figcaption`).
why: The right alternative depends on purpose, not on pixels. Hiding images and re-reading the page is a quick test: if the page still makes sense, they were decorative.
check: `img:not([alt])` count 0 (`I1`); decorative has `alt=""`; `a > img[alt=""]` with no other link text fails; charts and infographics have an adjacent long description link.
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: Keep alt text short and meaningful: aim under about 150 characters, no "image of / photo of" prefix, no keyword stuffing, proper punctuation, descriptive file names as a fallback. When in doubt about a decorative-vs-informative call, add the description because users can skip it but cannot invent it.
why: Long alt text causes fatigue; screen readers already announce "image".
check: `img[alt]` with `alt.length > 150` or `/^(image|photo|picture|graphic) of/i` flagged; `alt` equal to file name flagged (`I1`).
source: https://web.dev/learn/accessibility/images (150 is the module's guideline, not a WCAG number, treat as soft).
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: Inline SVG is silent by default. Informative SVG: `role="img"` plus an accessible name (`<title>` inside, or `aria-labelledby`). Decorative SVG: hide it. SVG inside a link needs the name on the link, via visually hidden text or `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby` on the link, not on the path.
why: SVGs have no `alt`; without a role some AT skip them, and inside links they leave the link nameless.
check: `svg:not([aria-hidden="true"]):not([role="img"])` inside `a,button` with no text sibling fails; `a:has(> svg)` and `button:has(> svg)` have a non-empty accessible name (axe `link-name`/`button-name`).
source: https://web.dev/learn/accessibility/images and https://web.dev/learn/accessibility/test-automated. [engine note] The module sometimes uses `role=presentation` on decorative SVG; `aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"` is the stricter option the existing rules use.
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: Use real text rather than text baked into images (low-vision magnification pixelates it and AT cannot read it).
why: Accessibility and translation.
check: `visual`: OCR or manual scan of `img` heroes; flag any `img` whose natural alt equals long marketing copy.
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: Pre-recorded video needs captions (closed, so users can toggle and style them), a transcript (in-page, a linked accessible PDF, or a linked page), and an audio description where the visuals carry information. Audio-only needs a transcript. Do not rely on auto-captions for deaf users.
why: Captions are for deaf and hard-of-hearing users; transcripts cover deafblind and slow readers; descriptions cover blind users.
check: `video` has `track[kind="captions"]` (or captions on the hosted player) and a nearby link/section labelled "Transcript"; background video without audio: confirm `muted` and decorative.
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: Contrast: 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text and essential icons. The module's "large" threshold is 24px (18pt) or 18.5px bold (14pt); logos and decorative elements are exempt. Test over solid colours with tools, over gradients and images manually.
why: Low contrast is the most common failure; automation cannot measure it over images.
source: https://web.dev/learn/accessibility/color-contrast. [engine note] Exact WCAG large-bold threshold is 14pt = 18.66px; the module rounds to 18.5, use 18.66.
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: Do not communicate with colour alone: add text, icon, pattern or underline. Review the interface in grayscale as a quick check. Links inside text need a non-colour cue (underline is the default) or 3:1 contrast against the surrounding text plus an extra cue on hover and focus.
why: Roughly 1 in 12 men and 1 in 200 women have colour vision deficiency; low-light and glare do the same temporarily.
applies: links, status badges, charts, form states.
check: links within paragraphs: `text-decoration-line` underline OR contrast(link, parent text) >= 3 AND focus/hover adds a non-colour change; status chips contain text or icon, not only a coloured dot; grayscale screenshot comparison `visual`.
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: Honour user colour preferences: `prefers-color-scheme` for light/dark and `prefers-contrast` for high contrast; layers of media queries may be combined. Dark mode helps light-sensitive and migraine users.
why: Control for people with photophobia or contrast needs.
check: CSS has both queries (or `light-dark()` and a `prefers-contrast: more` block); Playwright `emulateMedia({colorScheme:'dark'})` and `contrast:'more'` re-run `A2`.
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: Never flash more than three times per second or below the general/red flash thresholds; test intense flashing or rapid light-dark transitions with PEAT. Non-essential moving, blinking or scrolling content that starts automatically and lasts over five seconds needs a pause/stop/hide control.
why: Seizure risk (photosensitive epilepsy) and distraction (ADHD).
applies: hero animation, carousels, tickers, autoplay video.
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. The module goes further than "remove motion on request": consider defaulting to the reduced state and enabling animation only on `no-preference`, and offer an in-page toggle (default off) because OS settings are phrased inconsistently (Windows: "Show animations").
why: You cannot predict which amount of motion triggers vestibular symptoms.
check: with `reducedMotion:'reduce'` no running CSS animation/transition other than opacity or colour; `document.getAnimations()` filtered by transform/translate is empty.
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: Set font sizes in relative units (rem, em, %) so browser text-size preferences work, limit the stack of emphasis styles (colour, bold, caps, italic), use headings and lists to chunk text, keep line length under about 80 characters (40 for logographic scripts), and avoid justified text.
why: Low vision, dyslexia and ADHD users lose their place in long lines and rivers of whitespace.
check: `html`/`body` font-size not a px value below user default; `getComputedStyle(p).textAlign !== 'justify'`; paragraph measure <= 80ch (`L5`).
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: When picking type, check for ambiguous glyphs (uppercase I, lowercase l, digit 1; b/d, p/q) and the `rn` vs `m` kerning trap; avoid all-caps-only and ornate or handwritten faces for body copy. Common typefaces read faster for many readers with reading disabilities.
why: Letter confusion reduces comprehension for people with dyslexia and low vision.
applies: body and UI faces, not necessarily display headlines.
check: `visual`: render "Il1 O0 rn m" specimen in the UI font; verify tight tracking does not merge r and n.
source: https://web.dev/learn/accessibility/typography. (opinion) The "choose common typefaces" advice is evidence-based but generic; see section 5.
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: Build forms from native elements (`form`, `input`, `select`, `textarea`, `fieldset`/`legend`), not `div role=form`. Give every field a visible, persistent `<label>` programmatically associated to it, and group related fields with `fieldset`+`legend`.
why: Native fields bring state, validation and keyboard behaviour; labels double as larger hit areas.
check: `A10`; axe `label`, `label-title-only`; `[role=form]` count 0; field groups (radios, address) inside `fieldset`.
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: A placeholder is not a label; it disappears and is not consistently exposed. Keep a real label.
why: Used up as soon as typing starts, fails memory, autofill and some AT.
check: `input[placeholder]:not([type=hidden])` without associated `label[for]`/`aria-labelledby` count 0.
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: Add `autocomplete` tokens (name, email, tel, bday, etc.) to fields about the user. Fields must not trigger a change of context (auto-submit, navigation) just by receiving focus or input.
why: Identify-purpose and fewer keystrokes help cognitive, motor and AT users; surprise context changes break expectations.
check: `A10`; `change` event on select does not navigate.
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: Give hints and format requirements through `aria-describedby` on the control in addition to the label; do not put them in `aria-labelledby`, which overrides the label text.
why: Description is read after name and role; labelledby replaces the label.
check: every id in `aria-describedby` resolves (`[aria-describedby]` targets exist); inputs with a `label[for]` do not also carry `aria-labelledby` unless it includes the label id.
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: Errors: mark the field in error, describe the problem in text, suggest how to fix it, and confirm success after resubmission. Place error messages where they can be reached with focus and live-region announcement.
why: WCAG 3.3.1, 3.3.3 and the module's own sequence: make the error known, then help correct it.
source: https://web.dev/learn/accessibility/forms. [engine note] The module suggests `aria-required` as the way to deliver custom error text; that is incorrect usage. Use `required` plus visible text, and `aria-describedby` for messages.
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: Link text must stand on its own: "Find out about our offers", not "click here" or bare "more". When a visible link text is not enough, add context without changing the visible words that voice users will speak.
why: Screen reader users list links out of context; voice users say the visible name.
check: link text blacklist `/^(click here|here|more|read more|learn more)$/i` flagged unless `aria-describedby`/`aria-labelledby` includes the visible text; axe `link-name`.
source: https://web.dev/learn/accessibility/test-manual and https://web.dev/learn/accessibility/test-assistive-technology. [engine note] See section 5 for the module's `aria-label` example that violates label-in-name.
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: Run the three test layers in order: automated (axe/Lighthouse), manual (keyboard walk with Tab, Shift+Tab, arrows, Space, Enter, Esc; visual checks including zoom and spacing; content checks), then assistive technology. Never treat a Lighthouse 100 as accessible.
why: Automation covers only a minority of success criteria and flags false positives.
check: pipeline stages `A1` (axe), keyboard script (`A3`,`A4`,`A15`), manual screen reader pass recorded in the ledger.
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: Pair screen readers with the browsers they were built for: JAWS (Chrome, Firefox, Edge), NVDA (Chrome, Firefox), Narrator (Edge), VoiceOver macOS/iOS (Safari), TalkBack (Chrome, Firefox), Orca (Firefox), ChromeVox (Chrome). Use element-list/rotor commands (landmarks, headings, links, form controls, tables) to verify structure.
why: Mismatched pairs show bugs real users will not meet.
check: manual; record pairing in test log.
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: Before building a widget, look for an established accessible pattern (Inclusive Components, GOV.UK Design System, USWDS, APG, Deque library, Accessible Components, MagentaA11y) and then still test it. Never paste "accessible" code and assume it fits.
why: Patterns assume particular browsers, AT, markup and content constraints.
check: process: note the reference pattern in the component spec; run the component keyboard contract (`A15`).
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: Attach accessibility annotations to design hand-offs: colour contrast pairs, button/link state set (default, hover, active, focus, disabled), skip link visible/hidden states, alt text for essential images, captions and transcript locations, heading levels, landmarks, tab order and initial focus, form labels/help/errors/success, accessible names.
why: Design-stage decisions prevent late bugs; developers cannot infer intent from pixels.
check: process; spec file has a "states" and "focus order" block per component (see `component-accessible-anatomy.md`).
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/accessibility

text: Apply `box-sizing: border-box` to `*, *::before, *::after` in the reset.
why: Default `content-box` adds padding and border to `width`, so `width:100px; padding:20px; border:1px` renders 142 px wide and overflows its parent.
check: Playwright: `[...document.querySelectorAll('*')].filter(e=>getComputedStyle(e).boxSizing!=='border-box').length` is 0 (allow replaced controls if intentional).
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/css

text: Let text containers size intrinsically: no fixed `height` on any box that holds copy; use `min-height`, padding or `aspect-ratio` on media instead.
why: An extrinsic size has a content limit after which text spills out of the border box; intrinsic sizing resizes with the content.
check: for every element with text, `scrollHeight <= clientHeight + 1` after injecting +40% text (stress `S7`); static scan for `height:` on `.card, .btn, p, h1-h6`.
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/css

text: Use unitless `line-height` (for example `1.5`), never a length or percentage, on anything that inherits.
why: A unitless value is recomputed per element from its own font size; a length is inherited as a fixed computed value and looks wrong on larger children.
check: static: authored `line-height` values match `^[0-9.]+$|normal|inherit`; computed `line-height / font-size` on `p`, `li`, `h1-h6` is in the ranges of the typography notes.
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/css

text: Size type and spacing with `rem`/`em` (and `ch` for measure); do not declare the root font size in `px`.
why: `px` text ignores the user's default font-size preference; relative units honour it.
check: static: `html{font-size:` is `%`, `rem`-free or absent, never `px`; `p, li { font-size }` not `px` in authored CSS.
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/css

text: Cap reading measure with `ch`: body copy `max-inline-size: 60ch` to `75ch` (the course example uses 60ch).
why: `ch` is the width of "0" in the rendered font, so the cap tracks the actual font and size.
check: Playwright: `p.getBoundingClientRect().width / (fontSize * 0.5)` approximates chars per line; assert 45-75 (`L5`).
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/css

text: Use `svh`/`lvh`/`dvh` (and `svw` family) instead of `vh` for anything tied to the visible mobile viewport; use `cqi`/`cqw` inside container-query components.
why: Mobile browser chrome appears and disappears without changing the classic viewport: `svh` is with chrome shown, `lvh` with it hidden, `dvh` tracks live.
check: static: bare `100vh` only as a fallback preceding a `dvh|svh` line (`L10`).
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/css

text: Space siblings with `gap` on flex or grid parents (or one-direction margins like `margin-block-start` via `> * + *` with a child combinator) rather than margins on both ends.
why: Vertical margins between block siblings collapse to the larger value, margins do not collapse in flex/grid, and `* + *` without `>` leaks into nested children. Percent padding and margin are always a percentage of the containing block's width, not height.
check: static: no `margin-top` and `margin-bottom` pair used for rhythm between siblings; visual regression at 320/1280.
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/css

text: Define spacing and gutter tokens once as custom properties (the course's example: `--gutter: 20px; --spacing: 1em`) and reuse them.
why: One definition cascades everywhere and can be overridden locally.
check: static: count distinct `padding/margin/gap` literal values in authored CSS is at most the scale length.
origin: web:https://web.dev/learn/css

text: Do not use `flex-direction: row-reverse|column-reverse`, `order`, or `grid-auto-flow: dense` to repair DOM order. Change the HTML.
why: Visual order changes but focus order and screen-reader order follow the DOM, so Tab jumps around the layout.

text: In flex rows that must wrap, set `flex-wrap: wrap` and size items with `flex: 1 1 <basis>`; remember the initial values are `row`, `nowrap`, `flex: 0 1 auto`.
why: With `nowrap`, items shrink to `min-content` then overflow; each wrapped line is its own flex container, so cross-line alignment is impossible (use grid for that).
check: `L1` no horizontal overflow at 320; items of equal rank align by grid only (`L12`).

text: Use `margin-inline-start: auto` (an auto margin) to split a flex group, not a spacer element; there is no `justify-self` in flexbox.
why: Flex items act as one group on the main axis; an auto margin absorbs the free space on one side.
check: visual; static: no empty `<div class=spacer>` inside flex containers.

text: For equal-width grid columns use `minmax(0, 1fr)` (or `repeat(n, minmax(0, 1fr))`), not bare `1fr`.
why: `1fr` is `minmax(auto, 1fr)`, so a long unbreakable token forces its column wider and the columns stop being equal; `minmax(0,1fr)` lets every track shrink to the share.
check: Playwright: inject a 40-character unbroken string into one cell, assert all column widths within 1 px (`S7`).

text: For responsive card grids use `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(100%, 16rem), 1fr))` [engine note: the `min(100%, ...)` guard is mine; the course shows `minmax(200px, 1fr)`]. Use `auto-fit` when you want the tracks of a short last row to collapse and stretch, `auto-fill` when you want empty tracks kept.

text: Align inner rows of sibling cards with `subgrid` (`grid-row: span N; grid-template-rows: subgrid`) instead of fixed heights or JS equalisation.
why: The nested grid inherits parent track sizing and gap, so headings, bodies and CTAs line up across cards whatever the copy length. [verified-C156: three cards with 1-line, 6-line and 3-line copy gave identical CTA `top` of 222.4 px; the same markup without subgrid gave 142.4/222.4/160.4.]

text: Write `grid-template-areas` as complete rectangles (no empty cells; use `.` for blanks) and redefine the whole property at breakpoints.
why: An incomplete or non-rectangular area string makes the entire declaration invalid and it is silently dropped.

text: Do not use `display: contents` to delete a wrapper that carries semantics (list, button, nav, table parts).

text: Never style with ID selectors; keep authored selectors at specificity `(0,2,0)` or lower; reach for `:where()` to zero out base and reset rules.

text: To override instead of escalate, move the rule later, put the third-party CSS in an earlier `@layer`, or use `revert-layer`; as a last resort repeat the class (`.btn.btn`).
why: `revert-layer` hides only the current layer's value so library defaults show again; repeating a class adds `(0,1,0)` without an ID but signals a design smell if frequent.
check: static: third-party stylesheets imported with `@import url() layer(vendor)`.

text: Do not assume a CSS-only comparison beats an inline style or `!important`: inline `style=""` does not add specificity (it is a separate step) and `!important` is a different origin.
why: Knowing the order (importance, origin, specificity, position) prevents specificity wars; in the source `:visited`/`transition` examples show order effects.

text: Style link states in LVHA order (`:link`, `:visited`, `:hover`, `:active`) and only with colour properties on `:visited`.
why: Later equal-specificity rules win; `:visited` is limited to colour, background-color, border-color, outline-color and SVG fill/stroke for privacy.

text: Use `:is()` to group, `:not()` to exclude, and `:has()` for parent state, remembering that `:is()` forgives bad arguments but `:has()` does not (one invalid selector, such as a pseudo-element, discards the whole rule) and `:has()` cannot nest.
why: Silent rule loss is a layout bug that no linter on the property line will catch.
check: Playwright: after load, each `:has()` rule's target matches in at least one state (`document.querySelector(sel)` non-null in a fixture); static: no `:has(` containing `::`.

text: For zebra striping or counts on filterable lists use `:nth-child(even of :not([hidden]))`.
why: Plain `:nth-child(even)` counts hidden rows, so two visible rows can share a colour.
check: fixture: hide row 2, assert visible rows alternate in computed background.

text: Nest at most 2-3 levels, write `&` whenever you mean a compound (`&:hover`, `&.is-open`) and put a type selector before `&` (`p&`, not `&p`). Nested rules and `@media`/`@container`/`@supports`/`@layer` can sit inside a rule.
why: Without `&` a nested selector is a descendant selector; the nested selector takes the specificity of the most specific parent selector in a list, so `#a, .b { & a {} }` weighs like `#a a`.
check: static: nesting depth at most 3; no `&p` token; no `#` selector in a nesting parent list.

text: Do not put pseudo-elements in a nested parent selector list and expect `&` to match them; nest the pseudo-element rule explicitly (`&::before`).
why: `&` cannot represent pseudo-elements.
check: static review of `blockquote, blockquote::before { & {} }` shapes.

text: Generated content must not carry meaning: any non-empty `content` string on `::before/::after` is exposed to screen readers, so use `content: ""` for decoration or the alt form `content: "\2192" / ""`.
why: Screen readers read the generated text; empty strings are skipped.

text: Register tokens that must animate or be type-checked with `@property` (`syntax`, `inherits`, `initial-value`); leave design tokens that are plain strings unregistered.
why: An unregistered property is an opaque token stream and cannot interpolate; a registered one with a typed syntax falls back to `initial-value` when given a wrong type.
check: static: each custom property referenced in a `transition`/`@keyframes` has an `@property` block.

text: Give `var()` a fallback for any token that may be unset in a component (`var(--x, <fallback>)`), and never feed a token of the wrong type into a property.
why: An invalid substitution yields `initial`/`inherit`, not the previous declaration (transparent background in the course example).
check: Playwright: for each design token used as `background-color`/`color`, computed colour is not `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)` unless intended (`H6`).

text: Set custom properties from JavaScript with `el.style.setProperty('--x', v)` and read them with `getComputedStyle(el).getPropertyValue('--x')`.
why: The course snippet writes `getComputedStyle(element).setPropertyValue(...)`, which does not exist and throws; computed style objects are read-only. [source bug, verify before copying any web.dev JS]

text: Remember `var()` cannot be used in media or container query conditions; use literal lengths or `em`/`rem` there.

text: Build fluid sizes with `clamp(min, rem + vw, max)`; the rem part is what makes the size respond to the user's font setting. Provide a static `font-size` line before it for pre-`clamp()` browsers (the cascade drops unknown values).
why: A pure `vw` size ignores user preference. [verified-C156: `clamp(1.125rem, 1rem + 1.2vw, 2.5rem)` computed 19.84 px at 320, 31.36 at 1280, 40 at 2560; doubling the root font size gave 47.36 px, a ratio of only 1.51, and an emulated 200% zoom (640 px viewport, DPR 2) also gave 1.51 in device pixels.] Any non-zero `vw` coefficient makes the 200%-zoom growth less than 2x, so the existing `A13` assertion "ratio >= 1.9" cannot be met by a fluid size; see section 5.

text: Check every `calc()`/`min()`/`max()`/`clamp()` for operator spacing and closing parentheses: `calc(100vw-2em)` is invalid, `-` and `+` need spaces.

text: Store brand colours as `oklch()`; derive hover, pressed and border variants with relative colour syntax (`oklch(from var(--brand) calc(l * 0.9) c h)`) or `color-mix(in oklab, ...)`; re-check contrast on every derived pair.
why: OKLCH lightness is perceptual, so a 10% change reads the same on every hue; the course warns that dynamic colours can break contrast.
check: Playwright contrast (`A2`) for default, hover, disabled-exempt, focus states; computed colours not transparent.

text: Remember hex alpha values: 50% = `80`, 75% = `BF`, 0% = `00`; prefer `rgb(0 0 0 / 50%)` or `oklch(... / 50%)` when you want readable code.
why: Hex alpha is base-16 of 255, so "50%" is not `50`.

text: Interpolate gradients in a perceptual space: `linear-gradient(in oklch, A, B)`; add `longer hue`/`increasing hue` only deliberately.
why: sRGB interpolation of saturated pairs passes through muddy greys; the default colour space for gradients and `color-mix()` is `oklab`.

text: When wide-gamut colours (`display-p3`, high-chroma `oklch`) matter, branch with `@media (color-gamut: p3)` and keep an sRGB-safe value as the default.
why: Out-of-gamut colours are gamut-mapped to something close, not clipped predictably.

text: Frosted glass: use `backdrop-filter: blur()` with a semi-opaque background colour so text stays legible when the filter is unsupported or disabled. Any invalid function inside `filter` invalidates the whole list.

text: Shadow selection: `box-shadow` for rectangles (clipped by `overflow: hidden` ancestors, takes `border-radius`), `text-shadow` for glyphs, `filter: drop-shadow()` for cut-out images and transparent PNG/SVG. Use several comma-separated layers rather than one heavy blur.
why: A box shadow follows the box not the pixels; `drop-shadow` follows the alpha mask but has no spread or inset.
check: visual; Playwright: shadow parent has no `overflow:hidden` unless the shadow is meant to be clipped.

text: Do not rely on shadows alone for borders or focus rings.
why: Windows High Contrast / forced-colors mode removes shadows and most backgrounds, leaving an invisible control.
check: emulate `forcedColors: 'active'`, assert controls keep a non-zero border or outline (`A18`).

text: Show focus with an `outline` (colour with contrast, `outline-offset` for breathing room); never `outline: none` without a replacement; use `:focus-visible` to avoid mouse-click rings. The course teaches `:focus` first and `:focus-visible` in the pseudo-classes lesson.

text: Make programmatic skip-link targets focusable with `tabindex="-1"` (for `<main id>`) and style the target (`:target` or `:focus`) so the jump is visible; add `scroll-margin-top` so it clears sticky headers.

text: Any `overflow: auto|scroll` region must be keyboard reachable: `tabindex="0"`, `role="region"` and `aria-labelledby`, plus a focus outline; an attribute-gated pattern (`[role][aria-labelledby][tabindex]{overflow:auto}`) enforces it.

text: Prefer `overflow: clip` over `hidden` when you only need clipping; remember `hidden`/`auto` create a block formatting context and a scroll container, and `visible` is the default because "never hide content".

text: Apply `scroll-behavior: smooth` only inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`; add `scroll-padding-top` for fixed headers and `scroll-margin` on targets.
why: Smooth scroll is motion. Note the course's snippet sets `scroll-behavior: auto` inside the `no-preference` block, which is the default and has no effect; write `smooth`. [source bug]

text: Use `overscroll-behavior: contain` on modal panels and nested scrollers to stop scroll chaining; treat `scroll-snap-type: ... mandatory` as risky and test that every item is reachable on small screens.

text: Truncate single lines with `overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap`; do not use it on text a user must read in full.
why: It needs all three declarations and works on one line only.

text: Use `z-index` from a named scale, and contain a component's stacking with `isolation: isolate`; remember `opacity < 1`, `transform`, `filter`, `will-change` create stacking contexts, and `z-index` needs a positioned element unless it is a flex/grid item.

text: Transition named properties; prefer `transform`, `opacity` (and individual `translate`, `scale`, `rotate`) over width/height/top/left. Use a different duration for enter and exit by setting `transition` on the hover/focus state as well as the base.

text: Wrap movement, scaling and large opacity changes in `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`; colour changes may stay (the course: "usually don't need" the guard); pause autoplaying keyframe loops under `reduce`.
why: Preference means less, especially unexpected, motion.

text: Name keyframes in lowercase, remember `animation-duration` defaults to 0s, use `animation-fill-mode: both` for reveal-in animations, and set `animation-timeline` after the `animation` shorthand when you use scroll timelines.

text: Clip and mask carefully: `clip-path` and `mask` change only what is painted (the box, float wrapping and hit-testing stay rectangular unless you add `shape-outside`); animate `clip-path` only between the same function with the same number of points; `path()` is px-only and non-responsive, `shape()` is responsive but not in Firefox (per the page).

text: Author in logical properties: `margin-inline-start|end`, `padding-block`, `inset-inline`, `border-inline-start`, `text-align: start|end`, `border-start-start-radius`, `max-inline-size`; use `vi`/`vb` instead of `vw`/`vh` when writing-mode may change.

text: Always end `font-family` with a generic family that matches the design (`sans-serif`, `serif`, `monospace`, `system-ui`); remember the browser falls back per character, not per string.
why: A missing generic falls back to the browser default (often a serif).

text: Declare `@font-face` once with `font-display`, `src: local() ... url(...woff2)` (local first), and `unicode-range` for subsets; numeric `font-weight` values other than 100-step multiples need a variable font.

text: Prefer `overflow-wrap: anywhere` over `break-word` when the container is a flex/grid item or shrink-to-fit; avoid `word-break: break-all` on prose.

text: Branch pointer-dependent UI on `@media (pointer: coarse)` / `(any-pointer: fine)`, not width; use `touch-action: manipulation` to drop double-tap-zoom delay and never set `touch-action: none` on the document.

text: Components that appear in several widths get `container-type: inline-size` (named, via `container: name / inline-size`) and `@container name (inline-size > 30em)` rules; use `cqi` units inside; do not put the query on the container itself, only on descendants.

text: Use a popover (`popover` attribute, `popovertarget`) for non-modal layers; use `popover="auto"` (default) for menus (light dismiss, one open at a time, Esc), `manual` for toasts, and avoid `hint` until it ships in all engines. text: Fonts: WOFF2 only; subset with `unicode-range`; as few families and files as possible (system fonts, one variable font if you need several weights/styles); inline the `@font-face` declarations in `<head>` (not the font files); preload only the one or two critical files (preload ignores `unicode-range` and should name a single format); preconnect with `crossorigin` for third-party font hosts; replace icon fonts with SVG.
why: A font is requested only when styling uses it, so discovery depends on the stylesheet; Chromium and Firefox block text up to 3 s, Safari indefinitely, unless `font-display` says otherwise. check: `F1-F3`: every `@font-face` has `font-display`; woff2 only; <= 2 families; number of preloaded fonts <= 2; font files transferred <= 120 KB (craft budget).

text: Choose `font-display` by priority: `optional` for performance and zero layout shift (font may not be used on first visit), `swap` for brand text only if the font arrives early, `block` rarely; mix them (swap for headings/brand, optional for body); add metric-adjusted fallbacks with `size-adjust`, `ascent-override`, `descent-override`, `line-gap-override`; always end the stack with a generic family.
why: `swap` has no block period but swaps late and shifts; `optional` has a 100 ms block and no swap; omitting the generic fallback falls back to the default serif.

text: Keep tasks under 50 ms: yield with `await scheduler.yield()` (fall back to `setTimeout`) after the UI update, defer non-critical work with `requestAnimationFrame(() => setTimeout(...))`, batch loops with a 50 ms deadline, and do not use `isInputPending()` (no longer recommended).
why: Anything longer blocks input and the next paint; yielding after visible work lets the frame present sooner. Await the yield: `forEach` does not wait.
check: Playwright: `longtask` observer during scripted interactions; count tasks > 50 ms = 0 after load settles; TBT <= 200 ms.
